+# =============================================================================
+# Makefile — MelT reproduction package
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+# Targets per paper float; `make check` preflights the current box.
+# =============================================================================
+PY ?= python
+PLATFORM ?= $(shell $(PY) -m melt.detect)   # auto-detect: h100/v100/m4pro/a18pro
+
+.PHONY: help check platform tasks paper aggregate tables figures diagram test clean
+help:                ## list targets
+	@grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## .*$$' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sort | \
+	 awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "}{printf "  %-12s %s\n",$$1,$$2}'
+
+check:               ## preflight: is THIS box ready to run? (deps, device, datasets)
+	$(PY) -m melt.preflight --platform $(PLATFORM)
+
+platform:            ## run all speedup/energy stages for $(PLATFORM)
+	$(PY) -m experiments.run --platform $(PLATFORM) --all
+
+tasks:               ## run all CUDA-only task stages (whisper,voxceleb,equivalence,spira)
+	$(PY) -m experiments.run --tasks --all
+
+# single stages, e.g.  make latency PLATFORM=v100
+latency energy external msweep batch v100_power: ## run one speedup stage
+	$(PY) -m experiments.run $@ --platform $(PLATFORM)
+
+aggregate:           ## merge results/raw/**/ -> results/aggregated/*.csv
+	$(PY) analysis/aggregate.py
+tables:              ## aggregated -> ../IEEE-Access/Paper/tables/*.tex
+	$(PY) analysis/make_tables.py
+macros:              ## aggregated -> ../IEEE-Access/Paper/generated/numbers.tex
+	$(PY) analysis/make_macros.py
+figures:             ## aggregated -> ../IEEE-Access/Paper/figures/*.pdf
+	$(PY) analysis/make_figures.py
+diagram:             ## compile the standalone TikZ schematic (Fig. 1) -> figures/
+	$(PY) analysis/make_diagram.py
+paper: aggregate tables macros figures diagram ## full paper rebuild + consistency checks
+	$(PY) analysis/checks.py
+
+test:                ## CPU correctness tests (no GPU, no datasets)
+	$(PY) -m pytest -q tests/
+clean:               ## remove generated paper artifacts (keeps results/)
+	rm -f ../IEEE-Access/Paper/tables/*.tex ../IEEE-Access/Paper/figures/*.pdf

+# MelT — Reproduction Package
+
+Reproducibility code for **"MelT: A Portable, Single-GEMM Mel Audio Frontend via Non-Uniform DFT with Measured Latency and Energy Gains on GPUs"** (IEEE Access; arXiv:2606.01009).
+Camargo & Finger, University of São Paulo.
+
+MelT reformulates the conventional STFT → power → Mel pipeline as a **single
+dense GEMM** (a Mel-spaced NDFT projection). This package regenerates every
+table and figure in the paper from raw measurements.
+
+## Two-line mental model
+- **Each of the 4 boxes** runs one command — `./reproduce.sh` — producing the
+  speedup/energy results for that platform.
+- **One CUDA box** additionally runs the task scripts (`reproduce_whisper.sh`,
+  `reproduce_spira.sh`, `reproduce_voxceleb.sh`, `reproduce_equivalence.sh`),
+  which are about accuracy/equivalence, not speedup, and are hardware-independent.
+
+Then, on any one machine that has gathered all results: `make paper`.
+
+## Quickstart
+```bash
+# 1) a clean env — gives a writable site-packages AND a `python` on PATH
+python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # or: conda create -n melt python=3.11 && conda activate melt
+
+# 2) make the `melt` package importable — pick ONE:
+pip install -e .                 # (a) editable install — needs a writable filesystem
+export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src        # (b) no install — works anywhere (HPC/parallel FS); see HPC note
+pip install -r requirements-cuda.txt    # or requirements-apple.txt ; + torch matching the host
+
+# 3) get the data (see "Datasets" below for SPIRA / VoxCeleb), then preflight + run
+bash data/download_librispeech.sh   # LibriSpeech test-clean (Whisper task)
+# Libri6000 corpus: get train-clean-100 (OpenSLR #12), then build it from the recipe:
+python data/build_libri_100_160.py --librispeech <path>/LibriSpeech/train-clean-100
+make check                       # preflight: is THIS box ready? (deps, device, datasets)
+./reproduce.sh                   # auto-detects platform → results/raw/<platform_id>/
+```
+
+> **HPC / parallel filesystems (Lustre, GPFS, NFS `/work`, …).** `pip install -e .`
+> writes package metadata into the source tree, which some shared filesystems
+> reject (`Operation not permitted`). Either (a) keep the **code on a writable FS**
+> (clone to `$HOME`, install there) and point `DATASETS_DIR=/PATH/TO/datasets` at
+> your data on `/work`; or (b) **run without installing** — from the repo root:
+> ```bash
+> export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src        # inherited by the task subprocesses too
+> python -m melt.preflight --platform h100
+> python -m experiments.run --platform h100 --all
+> python -m melt.env --platform h100 --out results/raw/h100/env.json
+> ```
+> `make`/`reproduce.sh` call `python`, so ensure one is on PATH (a venv/conda env
+> provides it) or use the `python -m …` form above. `DATASETS_DIR` is honoured
+> everywhere, so data may live on `/work` regardless of where the code lives.
+
+## Datasets
+All data lives under `datasets/` (gitignored). Set `DATASETS_DIR=/path/to/scratch`
+to keep it elsewhere — every script and preflight follows it. Only LibriSpeech is
+needed on every box; SPIRA and VoxCeleb are only for their CUDA tasks.
+
+| Dataset | Needed for | How to get it |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Libri6000\_100\_160** (derived) | speedup/energy/external/equivalence/msweep/batch (all boxes) | **rebuilt from public LibriSpeech train-clean-100** (OpenSLR #12) with `python data/build_libri_100_160.py --librispeech <train-clean-100>`; recipe `data/libri_100_160_sources.csv`, sha256 `data/libri_100_160_checksums.csv` |
+| **LibriSpeech** test-clean | Whisper task (CUDA box) | `bash data/download_librispeech.sh` (OpenSLR) |
+| **SPIRA** (public, CC BY-SA 4.0) | Table VII (SPIRA) | download from `github.com/SPIRA-COVID19/SPIRA-ACL2021` into `datasets/spira/` — layout + citation in `data/spira.md` |
+| **VoxCeleb1** (research license) | Table VIII (VoxCeleb) | obtain from the VoxCeleb project into `datasets/voxceleb1/` + a `manifest.csv` (`path,gender,speaker`) — see `data/voxceleb.md` |
+
+Expected tree, licenses, and a full step-by-step are in `datasets/README.md`,
+`docs/AVAILABILITY.md`, and the end-to-end recipe `docs/REPRODUCE.md`.
+
+CUDA box, once each (needs the task datasets above + `pip install -r requirements-tasks.txt`):
+```bash
+./reproduce_whisper.sh   ./reproduce_voxceleb.sh   ./reproduce_equivalence.sh
+./reproduce_spira.sh --train   # SPIRA is public (CC BY-SA 4.0); --train builds the checkpoints, then evaluates
+```
+Assemble the paper artifacts (after collecting all results/raw/* subtrees):
+```bash
+make paper               # aggregate -> tables + figures ; then analysis/checks.py
+```
+
+## Statistical methodology
+The downstream comparisons report effect sizes and significance, not point estimates alone:
+
+- **SPIRA (Table VII):** Accuracy, Precision, Sensitivity, Specificity, $F_1$, ROC-AUC,
+  PR-AUC at **window and patient level**; **McNemar** (with odds ratio); **DeLong's test**
+  on the ROC-AUC difference; and **patient-clustered paired-bootstrap** CIs for Acc/$F_1$/AUC
+  (windows correlate within patient, so the patient-clustered CI is the honest unit).
+- **Whisper (Table IX):** per-speaker **TOST** equivalence with **Holm–Bonferroni**
+  correction across the model family (family-wise error control).
+- **Latency / speedup (Tables IV, X):** the timing harness keeps the 20 trial-medians, so
+  each headline speedup is reported with a **bootstrap 90% CI** ($\times[\,\text{lo},\text{hi}\,]$);
+  the latency figure shows the per-trial IQR as error bars.
+- **Power/energy (Table IV):** per-platform power and energy reported as median with a 90% CI;
+  the V100 power-inversion has its own 4-rep $\pm$std controlled measurement.
+
+**Multi-seed robustness (`--seeds`).** To show a downstream gain is not a single-training-run
+artefact, train/evaluate across seeds and report **mean $\pm$ std** plus a **Wilcoxon
+signed-rank** paired test on the per-seed MFCCT$-$MFCC differences:
+```bash
+./reproduce_spira.sh    --train --seeds 43,44,45,46,49   # checkpoints/seed_<s>/ ; spira_seeds*.csv
+./reproduce_voxceleb.sh         --seeds 43,44,45,46,49   # voxceleb_seeds*.csv
+```
+Omitting `--seeds` runs the standard single-seed evaluation. `make paper` renders the
+multi-seed summary as `table_seeds.tex`.
+
+## Layout
+| Path | What |
+|---|---|
+| `src/melt/` | the library (MelT+MFCCT in `melt.py`, DSP, timing, power, stats, preflight) |
+| `experiments/` | thin runners: config in, `results/raw/` out |
+| `analysis/` | results → `paper/tables/*.tex` and `paper/figures/*.pdf` |
+| `configs/` | protocol defaults, per-platform, per-experiment, `preflight.yaml` |
+| `data/` | how to fetch/prepare data | `datasets/` | where data lives (gitignored) |
+| `results/raw/<id>/` | per-platform; `results/raw/tasks/` CUDA-only task results |
+| `docs/` | `MANIFEST.md` (float→command→output), `PROTOCOL.md`, `RUN_*.md` |
+| `native/` | **experimental lab** — native Apple MelT in MPSGraph/Metal (no Python, no torch); an edge-execution playground, **not part of the paper** (the cross-platform results stay on PyTorch for an apples-to-apples comparison) |
+
+See `docs/MANIFEST.md` for the exact command behind every paper float.
+
+## License
+Code: MIT (`LICENSE`). Figures/CSV artifacts: CC-BY-4.0 (`LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0`).

+# =============================================================================
+# analysis/aggregate.py — merge results/raw/**/ -> results/aggregated/*.csv
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Each per-platform file (results/raw/<id>/<stage>.csv) is concatenated with a
+# `platform` column; task files (results/raw/tasks/) are copied as canonical.
+# The aggregated CSVs are the committed, platform-agnostic inputs to the tables.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Merge per-platform + task raw results into canonical aggregated CSVs."""
+import csv
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+RAW = ROOT / "results" / "raw"
+AGG = ROOT / "results" / "aggregated"
+PLATFORMS = ["h100", "v100", "m4pro", "a18pro"]
+
+
+def _concat(stage):
+    """Concatenate results/raw/<platform>/<stage>.csv across platforms."""
+    rows, header = [], None
+    for p in PLATFORMS:
+        f = RAW / p / f"{stage}.csv"
+        if not f.exists():
+            continue
+        with open(f) as fh:
+            r = list(csv.reader(fh))
+        header = r[0]; rows += r[1:]
+    if header:
+        with open(AGG / f"{stage}.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
+            w = csv.writer(fh); w.writerow(header); w.writerows(rows)
+        print(f"  aggregated {stage}.csv  ({len(rows)} rows)")
+
+
+def _copy_tasks():
+    """Copy CUDA-task results verbatim (already platform-agnostic)."""
+    tdir = RAW / "tasks"
+    for f in tdir.glob("*.csv"):
+        (AGG / f.name).write_text(f.read_text())
+        print(f"  copied {f.name}")
+
+
+def _environment():
+    """Roll per-platform env.json sidecars into environment.csv (Table XIII)."""
+    rows = []
+    for p in PLATFORMS:
+        f = RAW / p / "env.json"
+        if f.exists():
+            d = json.loads(f.read_text())
+            rows.append([p, d.get("os"), d.get("python"), d.get("torch"),
+                         d.get("mlx"), d.get("gpu")])
+    if rows:
+        with open(AGG / "environment.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
+            w = csv.writer(fh)
+            w.writerow(["platform", "os", "python", "torch", "mlx", "gpu"]); w.writerows(rows)
+        print("  aggregated environment.csv")
+
+
+def main():
+    AGG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for s in ["latency", "energy", "external", "msweep", "batch", "mlx", "v100_power", "speedup"]:
+        _concat(s)
+    _copy_tasks(); _environment()
+    print("aggregate: done")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# =============================================================================
+# analysis/checks.py — numerical-consistency guard over the aggregated results
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Asserts the paper's invariants so a bad run can't slip into the tables:
+#   * energy_pt_mj == power * latency per row (the retained P-bar*t-bar column)
+#   * direct counter energy corroborates the estimate (WARN; counter >= estimate
+#     is expected since it also captures inter-call gaps)
+#   * cross-table agreement (msweep M=80 == telemetry H100 speedup)
+#   * speedups monotone in M ; ranges sane
+# Exits non-zero on any hard violation.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Consistency assertions over results/aggregated/*.csv (run by `make paper`)."""
+import csv
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+AGG = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "results" / "aggregated"
+
+
+def _read(name):
+    f = AGG / name
+    return list(csv.DictReader(open(f))) if f.exists() else []
+
+
+def check_energy_consistency(tol=0.03):
+    """energy_pt_mj ≈ power_w * latency_ms — the retained P-bar*t-bar cross-check
+    column must equal its definition (a guard that the column is computed right)."""
+    bad = []
+    for r in _read("energy.csv"):
+        e = float(r["energy_pt_mj"]); pe = float(r["power_w"]) * float(r["latency_ms"])
+        if e and abs(e - pe) / e > tol:
+            bad.append((r["platform"], r["frontend"], e, pe))
+    return bad
+
+
+def check_energy_agreement(neg_tol=0.15, pos_tol=0.50):
+    """Direct counter energy should corroborate the P-bar*t-bar estimate.
+
+    Counter >= estimate is EXPECTED (the counter also captures inter-call
+    dispatch/sync gaps that t-bar omits), so we only warn when the counter falls
+    *below* the estimate by >neg_tol (a red flag) or overshoots by >pos_tol
+    (worth investigating). Returns rows as (platform, frontend, meas, est, %).
+    """
+    flagged = []
+    for r in _read("energy.csv"):
+        if r.get("method") != "nvml_counter":   # independent cross-check only on NVIDIA
+            continue
+        meas, est = float(r["energy_measured_mj"]), float(r["energy_pt_mj"])
+        if not meas or not est:
+            continue
+        rel = (meas - est) / meas
+        if rel < -neg_tol or rel > pos_tol:
+            flagged.append((r["platform"], r["frontend"], meas, est, round(rel * 100, 1)))
+    return flagged
+
+
+def check_msweep_monotone():
+    """MelT speedup should fall monotonically as M grows (H100)."""
+    rows = [r for r in _read("msweep.csv") if r["platform"] == "h100"]
+    sp = [float(r["speedup"]) for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: int(r["n_mels"]))]
+    return sp == sorted(sp, reverse=True)
+
+
+def main():
+    fails, warns = [], []
+    bad = check_energy_consistency()
+    if bad:
+        fails.append(f"energy_pt != power*latency: {bad}")
+    dis = check_energy_agreement()
+    if dis:
+        warns.append(f"counter vs P*t disagreement beyond tol: {dis}")
+    if _read("msweep.csv") and not check_msweep_monotone():
+        fails.append("msweep speedup not monotone in M")
+    for w in warns:
+        print("  WARN:", w)
+    if fails:
+        print("CHECKS FAILED:"); [print("  -", f) for f in fails]; sys.exit(1)
+    print("checks: all invariants hold ✓")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# =============================================================================
+# analysis/make_diagram.py — compile the standalone TikZ schematic (Fig. 1) to PDF.
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+# License: MIT.
+#
+# The conceptual MFCC-vs-MFCCT pipeline diagram is hand-authored TikZ (not data-
+# driven), but its PDF is built here so `make paper` regenerates EVERY artifact the
+# manuscript consumes -- no hand-compiled figures. Source .tex lives next to the
+# manuscript in IEEE-Access/Paper/; the PDF lands in IEEE-Access/Paper/figures/.
+# tikz cannot be loaded inside ieeeaccess.cls, so the figure is a standalone doc.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Build the standalone TikZ schematic into IEEE-Access/Paper/figures/."""
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+PAPER = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1].parent / "IEEE-Access" / "Paper"
+SRC = PAPER / "figure_pipeline_mfcc_mfcct.tex"
+OUT = PAPER / "figures"
+
+
+def main():
+    if not SRC.exists():
+        print(f"  skip: {SRC.name} not found"); return
+    if shutil.which("pdflatex") is None:
+        print("  skip: pdflatex not available (install TeX Live to build Fig. 1)"); return
+    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        r = None
+        for _ in range(2):           # 2 passes for a stable standalone bounding box
+            r = subprocess.run(
+                ["pdflatex", "-interaction=nonstopmode", "-halt-on-error",
+                 "-output-directory", td, str(SRC)],
+                cwd=SRC.parent, capture_output=True, text=True)
+        pdf = Path(td) / (SRC.stem + ".pdf")
+        if r is None or r.returncode != 0 or not pdf.exists():
+            sys.stderr.write((r.stdout if r else "") + "\n")
+            print(f"  FAILED to compile {SRC.name}"); sys.exit(1)
+        shutil.copy(pdf, OUT / pdf.name)
+        print(f"  wrote {pdf.name}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# =============================================================================
+# analysis/make_figures.py — aggregated CSV -> paper/figures/*.pdf
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+# Vector PDF at IEEE single-column width, colourblind-safe palette. One function
+# per figure, each reading exactly the aggregated CSV(s) it needs. Figures whose
+# inputs are absent are skipped, so partial result sets still build.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Generate the paper's figures from results/aggregated/*.csv."""
+import csv
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+AGG = ROOT / "results" / "aggregated"
+# Paper artifacts reside with the manuscript in IEEE-Access/Paper/ (sibling of melt/).
+OUT = ROOT.parent / "IEEE-Access" / "Paper" / "figures"
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))        # for melt.roofline (single source of peaks)
+
+PLATS = [("h100", "H100"), ("v100", "V100"), ("m4pro", "M4 Pro"), ("a18pro", "A18 Pro")]
+C_BASE, C_MELT = "#0072B2", "#E69F00"        # colourblind-safe (blue baseline, orange MelT)
+plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 8, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
+
+
+def _read(name):
+    f = AGG / name
+    return list(csv.DictReader(open(f))) if f.exists() else None
+
+
+def _save(fig, name):
+    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(OUT / name); plt.close(fig)
+    print(f"  wrote {name}")
+
+
+def _longest_dur(rows):
+    return max(int(float(r["secs"])) for r in rows) if rows else None
+
+
+def fig_latency():
+    """Fig 2 — MelT vs STFT+Mel latency per platform (longest clip), log scale."""
+    rows = _read("latency.csv")
+    if not rows:
+        return
+    dur = _longest_dur(rows)
+    lat = {}
+    for r in rows:
+        if int(float(r["secs"])) == dur and r["frontend"] in ("melt", "stft_mel"):
+            lat.setdefault(r["platform"], {})[r["frontend"]] = (
+                float(r["median_ms"]), float(r["p25_ms"]), float(r["p75_ms"]))
+    pids = [pid for pid, lab in PLATS if pid in lat]
+    labs = [lab for pid, lab in PLATS if pid in lat]
+    melt = [lat[pid]["melt"][0] for pid in pids]
+    stft = [lat[pid]["stft_mel"][0] for pid in pids]
+
+    def _err(fe):           # asymmetric IQR [median-p25, p75-median] error bars
+        return np.array([[lat[pid][fe][0] - lat[pid][fe][1] for pid in pids],
+                         [lat[pid][fe][2] - lat[pid][fe][0] for pid in pids]])
+
+    x = np.arange(len(labs)); w = 0.38
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.4))
+    ax.bar(x - w/2, stft, w, label="STFT+Mel", color=C_BASE,

+# =============================================================================
+# analysis/make_tables.py — aggregated CSV -> paper/tables/*.tex (Tables IV-XIII)
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+# License: MIT.
+#
+# One read->format function per table; each reads exactly the aggregated CSV(s)
+# named in docs/MANIFEST.md and emits booktabs LaTeX (no vertical rules).
+# Derived factors (speedup, energy reduction) are computed from full precision.
+# Tables whose CSVs are absent are skipped, so partial result sets still build.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Generate the paper's LaTeX tables from results/aggregated/*.csv."""
+import csv
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+AGG = ROOT / "results" / "aggregated"
+# Paper artifacts reside with the manuscript in IEEE-Access/Paper/ (sibling of melt/).
+OUT = ROOT.parent / "IEEE-Access" / "Paper" / "tables"
+PLATS = [("h100", "H100"), ("v100", "V100"), ("m4pro", "M4 Pro"), ("a18pro", "A18 Pro")]
+
+
+def _read(name):
+    f = AGG / name
+    if not f.exists():
+        return None
+    with open(f) as fh:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(fh))
+
+
+def _write(fname, body, caption):
+    (OUT / fname).write_text(
+        f"% {caption}\n% Auto-generated by analysis/make_tables.py\n{body}\n")
+    print(f"  wrote {fname}")
+
+
+def _pivot_energy():
+    """energy.csv -> e[platform][frontend] = {lat, pow, en}."""
+    rows = _read("energy.csv")
+    if not rows:
+        return None
+    e = {}
+    for r in rows:
+        d = {"lat": float(r["latency_ms"]), "pow": float(r["power_w"]),
+             "en": float(r["energy_measured_mj"])}   # energy-v2: directly-measured
+        if r.get("power_ci_lo") not in (None, ""):     # optional power CI columns
+            d["pow_lo"], d["pow_hi"] = float(r["power_ci_lo"]), float(r["power_ci_hi"])
+        if r.get("energy_measured_ci_lo") not in (None, ""):    # optional energy CI columns
+            d["en_lo"], d["en_hi"] = float(r["energy_measured_ci_lo"]), float(r["energy_measured_ci_hi"])
+        e.setdefault(r["platform"], {})[r["frontend"]] = d
+    return e
+
+
+def _speedup_ci(pair):
+    """{platform: (speedup, lo, hi)} at the longest duration from speedup.csv."""
+    rows = _read("speedup.csv")
+    if not rows:
+        return {}
+    rows = [r for r in rows if r["pair"] == pair]
+    if not rows:
+        return {}
+    dur = max(int(float(r["secs"])) for r in rows)
+    out = {}
+    for r in rows:
+        if int(float(r["secs"])) == dur:
+            out[r["platform"]] = (_num(r["speedup"]), _num(r["ci_lo"]), _num(r["ci_hi"]))
+    return out
+
+
+def _lat_longest():
+    """latency.csv -> {platform: {frontend: median_ms at the longest duration}}.
+    The dedicated latency sweep (50/20/200) is the canonical latency source, so
+    Table IV, Fig. 2, and the prose all report the same speedup."""
+    rows = _read("latency.csv")
+    out = {}
+    by = {}
+    for r in rows or []:
+        by.setdefault(r["platform"], {}).setdefault(r["frontend"], {})[int(r["secs"])] = float(r["median_ms"])
+    for p, fr in by.items():
+        out[p] = {f: dd[max(dd)] for f, dd in fr.items()}
+    return out
+
+
+def table4_telemetry():
+    """Table IV — latency, energy, power (with CIs): MelT vs STFT+Mel, per platform."""
+    e = _pivot_energy()
+    if not e:
+        return
+    lat = _lat_longest()
+    sci = _speedup_ci("melt_vs_stft")
+    lines = ["\\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}", "\\toprule",
+             "Platform & Latency (ms) & Speedup & Energy (mJ) & Energy & "
+             "STFT Power (W) & MelT Power (W) \\\\",
+             " & STFT+Mel / MelT & & STFT+Mel / MelT & Reduction & & \\\\",
+             "\\midrule"]
+    for pid, lab in PLATS:
+        if pid not in e or "melt" not in e[pid] or "stft_mel" not in e[pid]:
+            continue
+        s, m = e[pid]["stft_mel"], e[pid]["melt"]
+        # latency + speedup from the dedicated latency sweep (latency.csv); energy
+        # and power stay from the controlled energy window (energy.csv).
+        ls = lat.get(pid, {}).get("stft_mel", s["lat"])
+        lm = lat.get(pid, {}).get("melt", m["lat"])
+
+        def powcell(d):
+            if "pow_lo" in d:
+                return f"${d['pow']:.1f}$ $[{d['pow_lo']:.1f}, {d['pow_hi']:.1f}]$"
+            return f"${d['pow']:.1f}$"
+
+        if pid in sci and sci[pid][1] is not None:        # bootstrap speedup CI
+            sp, lo, hi = sci[pid]
+            spcell = f"${sp:.2f}\\times$ $[{lo:.2f}, {hi:.2f}]$"
+        else:
+            spcell = f"${ls/lm:.2f}\\times$"
+        # energy-reduction interval from the per-frontend energy CIs (if present)
+        if "en_lo" in s and "en_lo" in m:
+            encell = (f"${s['en']/m['en']:.2f}\\times$ "
+                      f"$[{s['en_lo']/m['en_hi']:.2f}, {s['en_hi']/m['en_lo']:.2f}]$")
+        else:
+            encell = f"${s['en']/m['en']:.2f}\\times$"
+        lines.append(
+            f"{lab} & ${ls:.3f} / {lm:.3f}$ & {spcell} & "
+            f"${s['en']:.1f} / {m['en']:.1f}$ & {encell} & "
+            f"{powcell(s)} & {powcell(m)} \\\\")
+    lines += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}"]
+    _write("table4_telemetry.tex", "\n".join(lines), "Table IV — telemetry")
+

+def table10_mfcct():
+    """Table X — MFCCT vs MFCC latency/energy gains, per platform."""
+    e = _pivot_energy()
+    if not e:
+        return

+    lines = ["\\begin{tabular}{lcc}", "\\toprule",

+        lm = lat.get(pid, {})

+            latcell = f"${b['lat']/c['lat']:.2f}\\times$"  # fallback: energy.csv

+def table5_external():
+    """Table V — MelT speedup / energy reduction vs external libraries."""
+    rows = _read("external.csv")

+        return

+    for r in rows:

+    def cell(d, key):

+    def ecell(d):                                       # energy reduction + 90% interval

+
+    lines = ["\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}", "\\toprule",
+             " & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{TorchAudio} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{nnAudio} & librosa \\\\",
+             "\\cmidrule(lr){2-3}\\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\\cmidrule(lr){6-6}",
+             "Platform & Latency & Energy & Latency & Energy & Latency \\\\", "\\midrule"]
+    for pid, lab in PLATS:

+            f"{cell(nn,'latency_speedup_x')} & {ecell(nn)} & "
+            f"{cell(lr,'latency_speedup_x')} \\\\")

+    _write("table5_external.tex", "\n".join(lines), "Table V — external libraries")

+
+def _metric_table(csv_name, out_name, caption):
+    """Generic metric/value (+optional note) two-column table."""
+    rows = _read(csv_name)
+    if not rows:
+        return
+    lines = ["\\begin{tabular}{lr}", "\\toprule", "Metric & Value \\\\", "\\midrule"]

+def table9_whisper():

+def _num(v):

+            f"{lab.get(r['pair'], r['pair'])} & ${lm:.1f}\\!\\pm\\!{ls:.1f}$ & "
+            f"${rm:.1f}\\!\\pm\\!{rs:.1f}$ & {cm} & ${float(r['noninf_p']):.3g}$ \\\\")
+    lines += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}"]
+    _write("table8_voxceleb.tex", "\n".join(lines),
+           "Table VIII — VoxCeleb gender (multi-seed: baseline/proposed/drop-in + non-inferiority)")
+
+
+def table13_environment():
+    """Table XIII — software/hardware environment per platform (formatted for print:
+    OS and GPU strings are shortened; driver versions are reported in the text)."""
+    rows = _read("environment.csv")
+    if not rows:
+        return
+    plat = {"h100": "H100", "v100": "V100", "m4pro": "M4 Pro", "a18pro": "A18 Pro"}
+
+    def os_short(s):
+        s = s or ""
+        if s.startswith("Linux"):
+            g = s.split("glibc")[-1] if "glibc" in s else ""
+            return f"Linux (glibc {g})" if g else "Linux"
+        if s.startswith("macOS"):
+            parts = s.split("-")
+            return f"macOS {parts[1]}" if len(parts) > 1 else "macOS"
+        return s
+
+    def gpu_short(s):
+        s = (s or "").split(",")[0].strip()       # drop driver (reported in text)
+        s = s.replace("NVIDIA ", "").replace("-SXM2-32GB", " 32GB")
+        return s or "---"
+
+    lines = ["\\begin{tabular}{lllll}", "\\toprule",
+             "Platform & OS & Python & PyTorch & GPU \\\\", "\\midrule"]
+    for r in rows:
+        lines.append(f"{plat.get(r['platform'], r['platform'])} & {os_short(r.get('os'))} & "
+                     f"{r.get('python','')} & {r.get('torch','')} & {gpu_short(r.get('gpu'))} \\\\")
+    lines += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}"]
+    _write("table13_environment.tex", "\n".join(lines), "Table XIII — software environment")
+
+
+def main():
+    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    table4_telemetry()
+    table5_external()
+    table6_equivalence()
+    table7_spira()
+    table8_voxceleb()
+    table9_whisper()
+    table_seeds()
+    table10_mfcct()
+    table13_environment()
+    print("make_tables: done")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# =============================================================================
+# data/build_libri_100_160.py — ONE script, fully public: train-clean-100 in,
+# the paper corpus (Libri6000_100_160) out.  License: MIT.
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.
+#
+# INPUTS
+#   1. --librispeech : a CLEAN LibriSpeech **train-clean-100** download
+#                      (OpenSLR SLR12, CC-BY 4.0), i.e. <spk>/<chap>/*.flac .
+#   2. --manifest    : libri_100_160_sources.csv (shipped next to this script) —
+#                      the ordered list of train-clean-100 utterances that
+#                      compose each 160 s clip. This single file is the whole
+#                      recipe; it already bakes in the published ordering
+#                      (including the one corrupt source the authors' run
+#                      skipped), so the output is byte-for-byte the corpus used.
+#
+# OUTPUT
+#   --dst/0000.wav .. 0099.wav  (100 x 160 s, 16 kHz mono, PCM_16) +
+#   checksums.csv (sha256 of each clip).
+#
+# DETERMINISM / bit-exactness.  Each source utterance is decoded with
+# `librosa.load(.., sr=16000)`, cut/padded to 10 s, and rounded to PCM_16 via
+# libsndfile (soundfile) — exactly the path the original two-stage pipeline took
+# — then 16 such 10 s segments are concatenated and the 160 s clip is written as
+# PCM_16. No glob, no shuffle, no RNG: the manifest fixes everything.
+#
+# USAGE
+#   python data/build_libri_100_160.py --librispeech /path/to/LibriSpeech/train-clean-100
+#   # prove it matches a corpus you already have, bit-for-bit:
+#   python data/build_libri_100_160.py --librispeech /path/to/train-clean-100 \
+#       --verify-against /path/to/Libri6000_100_160
+# =============================================================================
+"""Build Libri6000_100_160 directly from a clean LibriSpeech train-clean-100."""
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import hashlib
+import io
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+
+SEG_SECS = 10        # each source utterance contributes a 10 s segment
+CLIP_SECS = 160      # each output clip is 160 s (= 16 segments)
+
+
+def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    p.add_argument("--librispeech", required=True,
+                   help="clean LibriSpeech train-clean-100 dir (<spk>/<chap>/*.flac)")
+    p.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, default=here / "libri_100_160_sources.csv",
+                   help="ordered source manifest (clip_id,seg_index,librispeech_relpath,...)")
+    p.add_argument("--dst", type=Path, default=Path("./Libri6000_100_160"))
+    p.add_argument("--sample-rate", type=int, default=16000)
+    p.add_argument("--verify-against", default=None,
+                   help="existing corpus dir; build in memory and compare bit-for-bit")
+    return p.parse_args()
+
+
+def _segment_int16(flac: Path, sr: int, seg_n: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Decode a source utterance to the exact PCM_16 a 10 s Libri6000 file stores."""
+    import librosa
+    import soundfile as sf
+
+    y, _ = librosa.load(str(flac), sr=sr)                       # float32, no resample at 16 kHz
+    seg = y[:seg_n] if len(y) >= seg_n else np.pad(y, (0, seg_n - len(y)), mode="constant")
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    sf.write(buf, seg, sr, format="WAV", subtype="PCM_16")      # libsndfile float -> int16
+    buf.seek(0)
+    return sf.read(buf, dtype="int16")[0]
+
+
+def _to_pcm16(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    return np.clip(x * 32767.0, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)
+
+
+def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
+        for blk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            h.update(blk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    a = parse_args()
+    sr, seg_n, target = a.sample_rate, SEG_SECS * a.sample_rate, CLIP_SECS * a.sample_rate
+    librispeech = Path(a.librispeech)
+    verify = a.verify_against is not None
+
+    # group manifest rows by clip, preserving order
+    clips: "OrderedDict[str, list]" = OrderedDict()
+    for r in csv.DictReader(open(a.manifest)):
+        clips.setdefault(r["clip_id"], []).append(
+            (r["librispeech_relpath"], int(r["src_start_sample"]), int(r["src_end_sample"])))
+    print(f"Manifest: {len(clips)} clips x {CLIP_SECS}s from {a.manifest.name}")
+    print(f"Source:   {librispeech}")
+    print(f"{'Verify:   ' if verify else 'Output:   '}{a.verify_against or a.dst}\n")
+
+    if not verify:
+        a.dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    from scipy.io import wavfile
+
+    cache: dict = {}
+    checks = [("filename", "sha256", "bytes")]
+    mismatches = 0
+
+    for ci, (clip_id, segs) in enumerate(clips.items()):
+        parts = []
+        for rel, s0, s1 in segs:
+            if rel not in cache:
+                src = librispeech / rel
+                if not src.exists():
+                    print(f"ERROR: utterance not found: {src}\n"
+                          f"       (is --librispeech the train-clean-100 dir?)")
+                    return 1
+                cache[rel] = _segment_int16(src, sr, seg_n)
+            parts.append(cache[rel][s0:s1].astype(np.float32) / 32768.0)
+        clip = _to_pcm16(np.concatenate(parts))
+        if len(clip) != target:
+            print(f"ERROR: {clip_id} has {len(clip)} samples (expected {target}).")
+            return 1
+
+        out_name = f"{clip_id}.wav"
+        if verify:
+            ref_path = Path(a.verify_against) / out_name
+            if not ref_path.exists():
+                print(f"  MISSING  {out_name}"); mismatches += 1; continue
+            _, ref = wavfile.read(str(ref_path))
+            if not (ref.shape == clip.shape and np.array_equal(ref, clip)):
+                d = (int(np.max(np.abs(ref.astype(np.int32) - clip.astype(np.int32))))
+                     if ref.shape == clip.shape else "len-mismatch")
+                print(f"  MISMATCH {out_name}  max|delta|={d}"); mismatches += 1
+        else:
+            wavfile.write(str(a.dst / out_name), sr, clip)
+            f = a.dst / out_name
+            checks.append((out_name, _sha256_file(f), f.stat().st_size))
+        if (ci + 1) % 10 == 0 or ci + 1 == len(clips):
+            print(f"  {'checked' if verify else 'built'} {ci + 1}/{len(clips)}")
+
+    if verify:
+        print("\nverification OK — every clip is bit-identical"
+              if not mismatches else f"\n{mismatches} clip(s) differ")
+        return 1 if mismatches else 0
+    csv.writer(open(a.dst / "checksums.csv", "w", newline="")).writerows(checks)
+    print(f"\nDone. {len(clips)} clips + checksums.csv -> {a.dst}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# data/download_librispeech.sh — fetch AND extract LibriSpeech test-clean into datasets/.
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.
+# Populates: datasets/librispeech/test-clean/ (Whisper) — libri6000 is built next.
+#
+# Idempotent and recoverable: safe to re-run. Skips work already done, validates the
+# archive, extracts an already-downloaded tarball, recovers a half-done extraction,
+# and never nests test-clean/ inside a leftover dir. Honours DATASETS_DIR.
+set -euo pipefail
+DST="${DATASETS_DIR:-./datasets}/librispeech"
+TARBALL="$DST/test-clean.tar.gz"
+URL="https://www.openslr.org/resources/12/test-clean.tar.gz"
+mkdir -p "$DST"
+
+# place_dir SRC -> $DST/test-clean, safely (mv into an existing dir would NEST).
+place() {
+  src="$1"
+  rmdir "$DST/test-clean" 2>/dev/null || true     # drop an empty leftover dest, if any
+  if [ -e "$DST/test-clean" ]; then
+    echo "ERROR: $DST/test-clean already exists and is not empty; refusing to overwrite." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  mv "$src" "$DST/test-clean"
+}
+
+# normalize: an empty test-clean/ left by a failed/manual run would cause nesting.
+if [ -d "$DST/test-clean" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A "$DST/test-clean" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+  rmdir "$DST/test-clean"
+fi
+
+# 0) already extracted (non-empty)? nothing to do.
+if [ -d "$DST/test-clean" ]; then
+  echo "already present -> $DST/test-clean"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# 0.5) recover a prior run that extracted into LibriSpeech/ but didn't move it.
+if [ -d "$DST/LibriSpeech/test-clean" ]; then
+  echo "found extracted LibriSpeech/test-clean — moving into place"
+  place "$DST/LibriSpeech/test-clean"
+  rmdir "$DST/LibriSpeech" 2>/dev/null || true     # ok if metadata .TXT files remain
+  echo "done -> $DST/test-clean"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# 1) a stale/corrupt tarball can never be repaired by resuming onto it — drop it.
+if [ -f "$TARBALL" ] && ! gzip -t "$TARBALL" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "existing $TARBALL is invalid/incomplete — removing and re-downloading"
+  rm -f "$TARBALL"
+fi
+# download only if the tarball is absent (-f: fail on HTTP error, no HTML error pages).
+if [ ! -f "$TARBALL" ]; then
+  echo "downloading $URL"
+  curl -fL "$URL" -o "$TARBALL"
+fi
+
+# 2) validate before extracting — guards against truncated / HTML-error downloads
+#    (the usual cause of "downloaded but didn't untar", e.g. no internet on the node).
+if ! gzip -t "$TARBALL" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "ERROR: $TARBALL is not a valid gzip archive." >&2
+  echo "       The download failed (often no internet on a compute node)." >&2
+  echo "       Fetch test-clean.tar.gz on a machine with internet, copy it to" >&2
+  echo "       $TARBALL, then re-run this script." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# 3) extract, then move LibriSpeech/test-clean -> test-clean (what preflight checks).
+echo "extracting $TARBALL ..."
+tar -xzf "$TARBALL" -C "$DST"
+place "$DST/LibriSpeech/test-clean"
+rmdir "$DST/LibriSpeech" 2>/dev/null || true       # ok if metadata .TXT files remain
+echo "done -> $DST/test-clean"

+# SPIRA (clinical COVID-19 respiratory — Table VII)
+
+SPIRA is **publicly available** (code + data) from the official project release;
+it is **not redistributed in this archive** because it is licensed **CC BY-SA 4.0**
+(share-alike), so we link to the source rather than re-host it.
+
+Download from the SPIRA project:
+- Code + dataset: **https://github.com/SPIRA-COVID19/SPIRA-ACL2021**  (CC BY-SA 4.0)
+- Project page: **https://spira.ime.usp.br/**
+
+Place it under `datasets/spira/` so the layout matches what the runner expects
+(map the SPIRA-ACL2021 metadata/audio onto these names):
+```
+datasets/spira/
+├── metadata_train.csv
+├── metadata_test.csv
+├── pacientes/...                     # patient recordings (16 kHz) — paths per the CSV file_path column
+├── controle/...                      # control recordings (16 kHz)
+└── checkpoints/                      # trained models (or produce them with --train)
+    ├── spira_final_model.pth         # MFCC baseline
+    └── spira_mfcct_final_model.pth   # MFCCT
+```
+The metadata CSVs reference audio via a `file_path` column like
+`pacientes/PTT-….wav` / `controle/….wav`; the loader resolves each as
+`datasets/spira/<file_path>`, so place the recordings under those two folders
+exactly as the CSVs name them (no separate `audio/` folder).
+DSP config matches the SPIRA paper: 16 kHz, 400 ms window, hop 160, 1200 FFT,
+40 MFCC, 4 s windowing.
+
+Run on a CUDA box:
+```bash
+./reproduce_spira.sh --train     # train MFCC + MFCCT, then evaluate
+./reproduce_spira.sh             # evaluate only (uses existing checkpoints)
+```
+
+Cite the dataset: E. Casanova, L. Gris, A. Camargo, et al., "Deep Learning
+against COVID-19: Respiratory Insufficiency Detection in Brazilian Portuguese
+Speech," Findings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021, pp. 625–633.
+
+Availability statement (paper): "The SPIRA dataset and code (Casanova et al.,
+2021) are publicly available under CC BY-SA 4.0 at
+github.com/SPIRA-COVID19/SPIRA-ACL2021."

+# REPRODUCE — end-to-end recipe
+
+A literal, step-by-step walkthrough to regenerate every table and figure in
+**"MelT: A Portable, Single-GEMM Mel Audio Frontend via Non-Uniform DFT with Measured Latency and Energy Gains on GPUs"** (Camargo & Finger, IEEE Access; arXiv:2606.01009) from raw
+measurements.
+
+**Mental model.** There are two kinds of result:
+
+- **Speedup / energy** (Tables IV, V, X, XI, XII; Figs 2, 3, 8). Hardware-specific,
+  so each of the four boxes runs `./reproduce.sh` once and contributes its own
+  rows (the `platform` column).
+- **Accuracy / equivalence** (Tables VI–IX; Figs 5, 6). Hardware-independent, so
+  the four task scripts run **once** on a single CUDA box.
+
+Then one machine that has collected every `results/raw/*` subtree runs
+`make paper` to build the tables and figures.
+
+The four platforms (`docs/HARDWARE.md`): `h100`, `v100` (CUDA + TF32) and
+`m4pro`, `a18pro` (Apple MPS — the A18 Pro runs on a MacBook Neo, same SoC as the
+iPhone 16 Pro, used as the smartphone-class proxy).
+
+---
+
+## Phase 0 — Prerequisites
+
+- Python ≥ 3.10, `git`, `curl`, `tar`.
+- Per box: an H100, a V100, a Mac mini (M4 Pro), and a MacBook Neo (A18 Pro). Any
+  subset works — you just get fewer platform rows.
+- One CUDA box (H100 or V100) for the accuracy/equivalence tasks.
+- Disk: LibriSpeech test-clean is ~350 MB; Libri6000 (derived) ~0.5 GB; VoxCeleb1
+  and SPIRA depend on what you download.
+
+By default everything reads/writes `./datasets`. To use a scratch disk, set
+`DATASETS_DIR=/path/to/scratch` once and every script and preflight follows it.
+
+---
+
+## Phase 1 — Get the code and install (every box)
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/augustocamargo/MelT.git
+cd MelT/melt                       # the reproduction package root
+
+pip install -e .                   # installs the `melt` package (numpy/scipy/soundfile/pyyaml/matplotlib)
+
+# add the extras for THIS box's role:
+pip install -r requirements-cuda.txt    # NVIDIA boxes (also installs torchaudio/nnAudio/librosa/pynvml)
+#   then install torch matching the host CUDA, e.g. H100:
+#   pip install torch==2.1.1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
+#   V100: pip install torch==2.3.1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
+
+pip install -r requirements-apple.txt   # Apple boxes instead (torch 2.12.0 + mlx 0.31.2)
+
+pip install -r requirements-tasks.txt   # ONLY on the CUDA box that runs the tasks
+                                        # (openai-whisper, jiwer, scikit-learn, pandas)
+```
+
+`pip install -e .` also exposes a `melt-check` console script (same as `make check`).
+
+---
+
+## Phase 2 — Preflight (every box)
+
+Confirm the box is recognised and has the deps/device/datasets each stage needs:
+
+```bash
+python -m melt.detect      # prints h100 | v100 | m4pro | a18pro
+make check                 # = python -m melt.preflight --platform <detected>
+#   or: ./reproduce.sh --check     (preflight only, runs nothing)
+```
+
+Fix anything it flags before proceeding. Re-run `make check` after the datasets
+are in place (Phase 3) — it also verifies the data layout.
+
+---
+
+## Phase 3 — Datasets
+
+### 3a. LibriSpeech + Libri6000 (needed on every box)
+
+`libri6000` backs latency/energy/external/equivalence/batch/msweep; `test-clean`
+backs the Whisper task.
+
+```bash
+bash data/download_librispeech.sh      # OpenSLR test-clean -> datasets/librispeech/test-clean/  (Whisper task; CC-BY 4.0)
+```
+
+The `Libri6000_100_160` corpus (100 x 160 s clips) is **not bundled** — it is
+rebuilt, byte-for-byte, from public LibriSpeech **train-clean-100** (OpenSLR #12,
+CC-BY 4.0). Download train-clean-100, then run the one-shot builder:
+```bash
+# train-clean-100.tar.gz from https://www.openslr.org/resources/12/ , extracted to
+#   <ls>/LibriSpeech/train-clean-100/<spk>/<chap>/*.flac
+python data/build_libri_100_160.py --librispeech <ls>/LibriSpeech/train-clean-100 \
+    --dst datasets/librispeech/libri6000
+```
+The recipe is `data/libri_100_160_sources.csv` (the ordered train-clean-100
+utterances per clip); integrity is `data/libri_100_160_checksums.csv`. Prove a
+build matches a corpus you already have with `--verify-against <dir>` ("every
+clip is bit-identical").
+
+### 3b. SPIRA — clinical COVID-19 respiratory (Table VII; CUDA box only)
+
+SPIRA is **publicly available** under **CC BY-SA 4.0**; it is not re-hosted in the
+archive (share-alike) — download it from the project and map it onto the expected
+layout (details and citation in `data/spira.md`):
+
+- Code + data: https://github.com/SPIRA-COVID19/SPIRA-ACL2021
+- Project page: https://spira.ime.usp.br/
+
+```
+datasets/spira/
+├── metadata_train.csv
+├── metadata_test.csv
+├── audio/...                       # 16 kHz recordings (utterance 1)
+└── checkpoints/                    # created by --train, or drop trained .pth here
+    ├── spira_final_model.pth       # MFCC baseline
+    └── spira_mfcct_final_model.pth # MFCCT
+```
+
+DSP config matches the SPIRA paper (16 kHz, 1200-pt window, hop 160, 40 MFCC, 4 s
+windows) and is already wired in `configs/experiments/spira.yaml`.
+
+### 3c. VoxCeleb1 — gender classification (Table VIII; CUDA box only)
+
+VoxCeleb1 carries a **research license** — obtain it from the VoxCeleb project
+(accept terms) at https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/data/voxceleb/. The classifier
+runs in manifest mode (`data/voxceleb.md`):
+
+```
+datasets/voxceleb1/
+├── manifest.csv                    # columns: path,gender,speaker
+└── wav/id1.../.../*.wav            # paths in manifest are relative to datasets/voxceleb1/
+```
+
+`manifest.csv` example rows:
+```
+path,gender,speaker
+wav/id10001/abc/00001.wav,m,id10001
+wav/id10002/xyz/00007.wav,f,id10002
+```
+
+---
+
+## Phase 4 — Speedup / energy on each box
+
+**Measurement protocol (important for reproducibility).** These kernels are
+sub-millisecond, so host contention skews the timings. Run each box **freshly
+booted**, **headless over SSH** (no interactive desktop/GUI session — it perturbs
+the measurement), and start only after background load has **settled below
+~5–10% CPU utilization**. On the NVIDIA datacenter GPUs (H100, V100), run the
+benchmark on a **dedicated GPU** — no co-resident jobs sharing the device. The
+harness adds 50 warmup iterations and reports the median of 20 trials × 200 calls,
+but a quiet, freshly-booted (or exclusively-allocated) machine is what makes those
+medians stable and comparable across runs.
+
+One command; it auto-detects the platform, preflights, runs every stage eligible
+for that hardware, and captures the environment:
+
+```bash
+./reproduce.sh                      # -> results/raw/<platform_id>/  (+ env.json)
+#   ./reproduce.sh --force          # recompute even if a stage's CSV exists
+#   ./reproduce.sh --platform v100  # override detection
+```
+
+Stages run per box (from `configs/platforms/<id>.yaml`):
+
+| Box | Stages |
+|---|---|
+| `h100` | latency, energy, external, msweep, batch |
+| `v100` | latency, energy, external, batch, **v100_power** |
+| `m4pro` | latency, energy, external |
+| `a18pro` | latency, energy, external |
+
+**V100 only** — lock the core clock first so the power profile (Fig 8) is a
+controlled, locked-clock FP32 measurement:
+
+```bash
+sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 1530
+./reproduce.sh
+```
+
+When a box finishes, copy its folder to the machine that will build the paper:
+
+```bash
+rsync -a results/raw/<platform_id>/  collector:/path/MelT/melt/results/raw/<platform_id>/
+```
+
+---
+
+## Phase 5 — Accuracy / equivalence tasks (run once on a CUDA box)
+
+These are about equivalence/accuracy, not speed, so they're hardware-independent
+and run a single time. Each script preflights its own data + deps and writes to
+`results/raw/tasks/`.
+
+```bash
+./reproduce_equivalence.sh          # Table VI, Fig 5   (needs libri6000)
+./reproduce_whisper.sh              # Table IX, Fig 6   (needs test-clean; downloads Whisper weights)
+./reproduce_voxceleb.sh             # Table VIII        (needs voxceleb1 + manifest)
+```
+
+### SPIRA — train then evaluate (Table VII, Fig 6)
+
+`--train` drives **both** vendored CasanovaCNN engines — the MFCC baseline
+(`spira_mfcc_model.py`) and the MFCCT variant (`spira_mfcct_model.py`) — through
+their cross-validated training, writing the two checkpoints, then evaluates the
+shared 606-window test set:
+
+```bash
+./reproduce_spira.sh --train        # train MFCC + MFCCT, write checkpoints, then eval
+#   ./reproduce_spira.sh            # eval only (uses existing checkpoints)
+#   ./reproduce_spira.sh --train --force   # retrain even if checkpoints exist
+```
+
+Notes:
+- Training is the longest step (full CNN training of two models); expect it to
+  dominate task wall-clock. It skips automatically if both checkpoints already
+  exist (use `--force` to retrain).
+- Evaluation runs under **bfloat16 autocast** to match training precision, so the
+  reported F1 / McNemar reproduce the paper's confusion matrices exactly; the
+  non-inferiority CI is **patient-clustered** (windows correlate within patient).
+
+If you only have checkpoints (no raw audio/training rights), drop them into
+`datasets/spira/checkpoints/` and run `./reproduce_spira.sh` without `--train`.
+
+Then push the task results to the collector box:
+
+```bash
+rsync -a results/raw/tasks/  collector:/path/MelT/melt/results/raw/tasks/
+```
+
+---
+
+## Phase 6 — Build the paper artifacts (collector box)
+
+Once every `results/raw/<id>/` and `results/raw/tasks/` is present on one machine:
+
+```bash
+make paper
+#   = analysis/aggregate.py     merge results/raw/**/ -> results/aggregated/*.csv
+#     analysis/make_tables.py   aggregated -> paper/tables/*.tex   (Tables IV–XIII)
+#     analysis/make_figures.py  aggregated -> paper/figures/*.pdf  (Figs 2, 3, 8 …)
+#     analysis/checks.py        numerical-consistency checks across the floats
+python analysis/make_graphical_abstract.py   # graphical abstract (external.csv + whisper_scaling.csv)
+```
+
+Individual steps are also available: `make aggregate`, `make tables`,
+`make figures`. `make clean` removes generated `paper/` artifacts but keeps
+`results/`.
+
+---
+
+## Phase 7 — Which command produces which float
+
+`docs/MANIFEST.md` is the authoritative float → command → artifact table. In short:
+
+| Float | Produced by | Reads |
+|---|---|---|
+| Table IV (latency+energy+power) | `./reproduce.sh` (each box) | `latency.csv`, `energy.csv` |
+| Table V (external libraries) | `./reproduce.sh` external stage | `external.csv` |
+| Table VI + Fig 5 (feature equiv) | `./reproduce_equivalence.sh` | `feature_equivalence.csv` |
+| Table VII + Fig 6 (SPIRA) | `./reproduce_spira.sh --train` | `spira_metrics.csv` |
+| Table VIII (VoxCeleb) | `./reproduce_voxceleb.sh` | `voxceleb.csv` |
+| Table IX + Fig 6 (Whisper) | `./reproduce_whisper.sh` | `whisper_scaling.csv` |
+| Table X (MFCCT) | `./reproduce.sh` (mfcct rows) | `energy.csv` / `latency.csv` |
+| Table XI (Mel-bin sweep) | `./reproduce.sh` msweep (H100) | `msweep.csv` |
+| Table XII (batch scaling) | `./reproduce.sh` batch (H100/V100) | `batch.csv` |
+| Table XIII (software env) | automatic per run | `environment.csv` |
+| Fig 8 (roofline) | `./reproduce.sh` v100_power + `make figures` | `v100_power.csv` |
+
+---
+
+## Minimal path (no GPU, just verify the code)
+
+```bash
+pip install -e .
+make test            # CPU correctness tests — no GPU, no datasets
+```
+
+This runs the unit tests for the MelT/MFCCT kernel and the statistics, confirming
+the install is sound before committing to the full multi-box run.
+
+---
+
+## Troubleshooting & notes
+
+- **`could not detect platform`** — pass `--platform {h100|v100|m4pro|a18pro}` to
+  `reproduce.sh` / `make`.
+- **Datasets elsewhere** — `export DATASETS_DIR=/PATH/TO/melt-data` before any
+  script; all paths follow it.
+- **Re-run a single stage** — `python -m experiments.run <stage> --platform <id>`
+  (e.g. `make latency PLATFORM=v100`); add `--force` to overwrite existing CSVs.
+- **Tasks are CUDA-only by design** — Whisper/SPIRA/VoxCeleb/equivalence will not
+  run on the Apple boxes; that is intentional (they measure accuracy, not speed).
+- **Whisper** downloads model weights on first run (needs network on the CUDA box).
+- Two in-code comments (`reproduce_spira.sh`, `spira_train.py`) still say
+  "access-gated" — SPIRA is in fact public (CC BY-SA 4.0); the authoritative note
+  is `data/spira.md`.

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/_common.py — shared helpers for the thin experiment runners
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+# Config loading/merge, audio loading (real clip or synthetic), and output
+# routing — so each runner stays a few lines of measurement logic.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Config + audio + output helpers shared by all experiment runners."""
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import numpy as np
+import yaml
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+CONF = ROOT / "configs"
+
+
+def load_config(stage):
+    """Merge configs/default.yaml with configs/experiments/<stage>.yaml."""
+    cfg = yaml.safe_load((CONF / "default.yaml").read_text())
+    f = CONF / "experiments" / f"{stage}.yaml"
+    if f.exists():
+        cfg[stage] = yaml.safe_load(f.read_text())
+    cfg["dataset_root"] = os.environ.get("DATASETS_DIR", cfg["dataset_root"])
+    return cfg
+
+
+def platform_device(platform_id):
+    """Return the torch device string for a platform_id."""
+    return "cuda" if platform_id in ("h100", "v100") else "mps"
+
+
+def load_audio(cfg, secs, prefer="librispeech/libri6000"):
+    """Load `secs` of a real clip from dataset_root, else synthesise.
+
+    Latency/energy of the fixed-shape ops are content-independent, so the
+    synthetic fallback yields identical timings when no corpus is present.
+    """
+    sr = cfg["sr"]
+    root = Path(cfg["dataset_root"]) / prefer
+    clips = sorted(root.glob("**/*.flac")) + sorted(root.glob("**/*.wav")) if root.exists() else []
+    if clips:
+        import soundfile as sf
+        w, r = sf.read(str(clips[0]), dtype="float32", always_2d=False)
+        if w.ndim > 1:
+            w = w.mean(1)
+        assert r == sr, f"{clips[0]}: {r} Hz != {sr}"
+        if len(w) < secs * sr:                       # tile short clips up to secs
+            w = np.tile(w, int(np.ceil(secs * sr / len(w))))
+        return w[: secs * sr].astype(np.float32)
+    return np.random.randn(secs * sr).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def corpus_clips(cfg, n=None, secs=None, prefer="librispeech/libri6000"):
+    """Yield DISTINCT real clips from the corpus (for content-dependent runs).
+
+    Used by feature-equivalence, which needs n separate replicates — unlike
+    load_audio() (one representative clip for content-independent timing).
+    """
+    import soundfile as sf
+    sr = cfg["sr"]
+    root = Path(cfg["dataset_root"]) / prefer
+    clips = sorted(root.glob("**/*.wav")) + sorted(root.glob("**/*.flac"))
+    assert clips, f"no corpus clips under {root} (see data/ to build librispeech/libri6000)"
+    if n:
+        clips = clips[:n]
+    for p in clips:
+        w, r = sf.read(str(p), dtype="float32", always_2d=False)
+        if w.ndim > 1:
+            w = w.mean(1)
+        assert r == sr, f"{p}: {r} Hz != {sr}"
+        yield (w[: secs * sr] if secs else w).astype(np.float32)

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/batch_scaling.py — throughput vs batch size -> Table XII
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# 4 s utterances batched 1..256; GPU compute time, H2D measured separately.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Batch-scaling: MelT vs STFT+Mel speedup, per-utterance latency, and energy."""
+from melt import MelT, timing, io, baselines, power
+from . import _common as C
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import torch
+    cfg = C.load_config("batch"); dev_str = C.platform_device(platform_id)
+    out = io.out_dir(platform_id); csv = out / "batch.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+    dev = timing.setup_torch(dev_str); sync = timing.make_sync(dev)
+    sp = cfg["spectral"]; clip_s = cfg["batch"]["clip_s"]
+    audio = C.load_audio(cfg, int(clip_s))
+    m = MelT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str, **sp)
+    X1 = m.frames(audio)                                  # [T, frame_len]
+    ref = baselines.make_reference(sp["n_mels"], sp["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                   sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"], "torch", dev_str)
+    # energy-v2 (Tier-2): directly-measured energy per batch point (same counter
+    # method as Table IV). Small trial count / window to bound the sweep's cost.
+    et = cfg["batch"].get("energy_trials", 5)
+    e_win = cfg["batch"].get("power_window_s", 1.0)
+    e_per = cfg["batch"].get("nvml_period_ms", 25)
+    rows = []
+    for B in cfg["batch"]["batch_sizes"]:
+        Xb = X1.unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, 1, 1)             # [B, T, frame_len]
+        mt = timing.bench(lambda: m(Xb), sync,
+                          n_timed=cfg["batch"]["runs"], n_trials=1,
+                          n_warmup=cfg["batch"]["warmup"])[0]
+        st = timing.bench(lambda: ref(Xb), sync,
+                          n_timed=cfg["batch"]["runs"], n_trials=1,
+                          n_warmup=cfg["batch"]["warmup"])[0]
+        if dev.type in ("cuda", "mps"):
+            me = power.measure_energy_stats(lambda: m(Xb), sync, dev, mt,
+                                            window_s=e_win, period_ms=e_per,
+                                            n_trials=et)["energy_measured_mj"]
+            se = power.measure_energy_stats(lambda: ref(Xb), sync, dev, st,
+                                            window_s=e_win, period_ms=e_per,
+                                            n_trials=et)["energy_measured_mj"]
+        else:
+            me = se = float("nan")
+        rows.append([platform_id, B, st, mt, st / mt, mt / B, se, me])
+    io.write_csv(csv, ["platform", "batch", "stft_ms", "melt_ms",
+                       "speedup", "melt_ms_per_utt", "stft_energy_mj", "melt_energy_mj"], rows)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "batch", platform_id, "configs/experiments/batch.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}")

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/energy.py — energy v2 at 160 s -> Table IV (energy/power), Fig 3
+#                          and the energy column of Table X (MFCCT)
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# DIRECTLY-MEASURED energy: NVML whole-board counter (CUDA) / integrated
+# timestamped powermetrics power (Apple, GPU-only), per call = window / n_calls.
+# P-bar*t-bar is retained as a same-window cross-check (energy_pt_mj). Headline
+# energy is GROSS; the idle baseline is captured so NET is derivable on demand.
+# Measures the same four front ends as latency.py so Tables IV and X share one
+# source:  spectral : melt, stft_mel    cepstral : mfcct, mfcc
+# =============================================================================
+"""Energy (NVML counter / integrated powermetrics) for MelT/MFCCT vs STFT+Mel/MFCC."""
+from melt import MelT, MFCCT, timing, io, baselines, power, dsp
+from . import _common as C
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import torch
+    cfg = C.load_config("energy"); dev_str = C.platform_device(platform_id)
+    out = io.out_dir(platform_id); csv = out / "energy.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+    dev = timing.setup_torch(dev_str); sync = timing.make_sync(dev)
+    sp, ce = cfg["spectral"], cfg["cepstral"]
+    ecfg = cfg["energy"]
+    win_s = ecfg["power_window_s"]; period = ecfg["nvml_period_ms"]
+    duration_s = ecfg["duration_s"]
+    n_trials = ecfg.get("n_energy_trials", 10)
+    idle_window_s = ecfg.get("idle_window_s", 5.0)
+    audio = C.load_audio(cfg, duration_s)
+
+    # spectral pair
+    m = MelT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str, **sp); Xs = m.frames(audio)
+    ref_s = baselines.make_reference(sp["n_mels"], sp["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                     sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"], "torch", dev_str)
+    # cepstral pair
+    mc = MFCCT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str,
+               n_mfcc=ce["n_mfcc"], n_mels=ce["n_mels"], frame_len=ce["frame_len"],
+               hop_len=ce["hop_len"], f_min=ce["f_min"], f_max=ce["f_max"])
+    Xc = mc.frames(audio)
+    ref_c = baselines.make_reference(ce["n_mels"], ce["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                     ce["f_min"], ce["f_max"], "torch", dev_str)
+    D = torch.from_numpy(dsp.dct_ii_matrix(ce["n_mfcc"], ce["n_mels"])).to(dev)
+
+    n_frames_sp = int(Xs.shape[0]); n_frames_ce = int(Xc.shape[0])
+    fns = [("melt", lambda: m(Xs), n_frames_sp),
+           ("stft_mel", lambda: ref_s(Xs), n_frames_sp),
+           ("mfcct", lambda: mc(Xc), n_frames_ce),
+           ("mfcc", lambda: ref_c(Xc) @ D.T, n_frames_ce)]
+    # Tier-2 robustness row (CUDA only): fused baseline via torch.compile, which
+    # fuses the elementwise stages. MelT's headline speedup stays measured vs the
+    # STANDARD pipeline; this is an extra row, not the primary baseline. The
+    # measure_energy_stats warmup amortizes the one-time compile.
+    if dev.type == "cuda":
+        ref_s_compiled = torch.compile(ref_s)
+        fns.append(("stft_mel_compiled", lambda: ref_s_compiled(Xs), n_frames_sp))
+
+    # idle baseline (once per device) for on-demand NET energy
+    idle = power.measure_idle(dev, idle_window_s, period)
+
+    header = ["platform", "frontend", "latency_ms",
+              "power_w", "power_ci_lo", "power_ci_hi",
+              "energy_measured_mj", "energy_measured_ci_lo", "energy_measured_ci_hi",
+              "energy_pt_mj", "agreement_pct",
+              "n_calls_window", "window_s_actual",
+              "idle_power_w", "idle_energy_mj",
+              "mj_per_audio_s", "mj_per_frame", "calls_per_s", "method"]
+    rows = []
+    for name, fn, n_frames in fns:
+        lat_ms = timing.bench(fn, sync)[0]
+        r = power.measure_energy_stats(fn, sync, dev, lat_ms,
+                                       window_s=win_s, period_ms=period, n_trials=n_trials)
+        e = r["energy_measured_mj"]
+        rows.append([platform_id, name, lat_ms,
+                     r["power_w"], r["power_ci_lo"], r["power_ci_hi"],
+                     e, r["energy_measured_ci_lo"], r["energy_measured_ci_hi"],
+                     r["energy_pt_mj"], r["agreement_pct"],
+                     r["n_calls_window"], r["window_s_actual"],
+                     idle["idle_power_w"], idle["idle_energy_mj"],
+                     e / duration_s, e / n_frames, 1000.0 / lat_ms, r["method"]])
+    io.write_csv(csv, header, rows)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "energy", platform_id, "configs/experiments/energy.yaml",
+                      extra={"idle": idle, "energy_method": rows[0][-1] if rows else None})
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}")

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/external_baselines.py — MelT vs torchaudio/nnAudio/librosa -> Table V
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Reports MelT's latency speedup AND energy reduction (ratios) over each library;
+# all libraries configured to the identical 80-bin log-Mel spec. librosa is a CPU
+# reference (latency only; GPU power samplers do not capture it).
+# =============================================================================
+"""External-library comparison (latency + energy ratios) for MelT vs libs."""
+from melt import MelT, timing, io, baselines, power
+from . import _common as C
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import torch
+    cfg = C.load_config("external"); dev_str = C.platform_device(platform_id)
+    out = io.out_dir(platform_id); csv = out / "external.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+    dev = timing.setup_torch(dev_str); sync = timing.make_sync(dev)
+    sp = cfg["spectral"]; ext = cfg["external"]; secs = ext["duration_s"]
+    audio = C.load_audio(cfg, secs)
+    m = MelT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str, **sp); X = m.frames(audio)
+    wav = torch.from_numpy(audio).to(dev)
+
+    fns, gpu = {"melt": lambda: m(X)}, {"melt": True}
+    for lib in ext["libraries"]:
+        if lib == "librosa":                       # CPU reference: latency only
+            fns[lib] = lambda a=audio: baselines.make_external(
+                "librosa", sr=cfg["sr"], n_fft=sp["frame_len"], hop=sp["hop_len"],
+                n_mels=sp["n_mels"], f_min=sp["f_min"], f_max=sp["f_max"], device=dev)(a)
+            gpu[lib] = False
+        else:
+            f = baselines.make_external(
+                lib, sr=cfg["sr"], n_fft=sp["frame_len"], hop=sp["hop_len"],
+                n_mels=sp["n_mels"], f_min=sp["f_min"], f_max=sp["f_max"], device=dev)
+            fns[lib] = (lambda f=f: f(wav)); gpu[lib] = True
+
+    # latency (all) + DIRECTLY-MEASURED energy (GPU libraries only; same counter
+    # method as Table IV so the two tables are consistent). librosa is CPU -> no
+    # device energy counter -> energy dropped (latency only), noted in the paper.
+    lat = {k: timing.bench(v, sync)[0] for k, v in fns.items()}
+    energy = {}
+    for k, v in fns.items():
+        if gpu[k]:
+            energy[k] = power.measure_energy_stats(v, sync, dev, lat[k],
+                                                   window_s=ext["power_window_s"],
+                                                   period_ms=ext["nvml_period_ms"])
+
+    rows = []
+    em = energy.get("melt")
+    for lib in fns:
+        if lib == "melt":
+            continue
+        if lib in energy and em:                       # GPU lib: ratio + 90% interval
+            el = energy[lib]
+            e_x = round(el["energy_measured_mj"] / em["energy_measured_mj"], 4)
+            e_lo = round(el["energy_measured_ci_lo"] / em["energy_measured_ci_hi"], 4)
+            e_hi = round(el["energy_measured_ci_hi"] / em["energy_measured_ci_lo"], 4)
+        else:                                          # librosa (CPU): latency only
+            e_x = e_lo = e_hi = ""
+        rows.append([platform_id, lib, round(lat[lib] / lat["melt"], 4), e_x, e_lo, e_hi])
+    io.write_csv(csv, ["platform", "library", "latency_speedup_x",
+                       "energy_reduction_x", "energy_reduction_lo", "energy_reduction_hi"], rows)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "external", platform_id, "configs/experiments/external.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}")

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/latency.py — latency vs duration  ->  Table IV (latency), Fig 2
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Times MelT/MFCCT and their conventional counterparts over 1..160 s using the
+# shared median-of-medians harness; writes results/raw/<id>/latency.csv.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Latency sweep over durations for MelT/MFCCT vs STFT+Mel/MFCC.
+
+Two front-end pairs at every duration, each timed against its conventional
+counterpart so both speedups (Table IV) and the cepstral gains (Table X) come
+from one run:
+  * spectral : MelT      vs STFT+Mel
+  * cepstral : MFCCT     vs MFCC ( = STFT+Mel -> DCT-II )
+"""
+from melt import MelT, MFCCT, timing, io, baselines, dsp, stats
+from . import _common as C
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import torch                                  # lazy: only needed at run time
+    cfg = C.load_config("latency"); dev_str = C.platform_device(platform_id)
+    out = io.out_dir(platform_id); csv = out / "latency.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+    dev = timing.setup_torch(dev_str); sync = timing.make_sync(dev)
+    sp, ce = cfg["spectral"], cfg["cepstral"]; rows = []; spd = []
+
+    # cepstral DCT-II matrix (MFCCT and the MFCC baseline share it)
+    D = torch.from_numpy(dsp.dct_ii_matrix(ce["n_mfcc"], ce["n_mels"])).to(dev)
+
+    for secs in cfg["durations_s"]:
+        audio = C.load_audio(cfg, secs)
+
+        # --- spectral pair: MelT vs STFT+Mel (frame 400) ---
+        m = MelT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str, **sp)
+        Xs = m.frames(audio)
+        ref_s = baselines.make_reference(sp["n_mels"], sp["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                         sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"], "torch", dev_str)
+
+        # --- cepstral pair: MFCCT vs MFCC (frame 1200) ---
+        mc = MFCCT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device=dev_str,
+                   n_mfcc=ce["n_mfcc"], n_mels=ce["n_mels"], frame_len=ce["frame_len"],
+                   hop_len=ce["hop_len"], f_min=ce["f_min"], f_max=ce["f_max"])
+        Xc = mc.frames(audio)
+        ref_c = baselines.make_reference(ce["n_mels"], ce["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                         ce["f_min"], ce["f_max"], "torch", dev_str)
+
+        cells = [("melt", lambda: m(Xs), Xs.shape[0]),
+                 ("stft_mel", lambda: ref_s(Xs), Xs.shape[0]),
+                 ("mfcct", lambda: mc(Xc), Xc.shape[0]),
+                 ("mfcc", lambda: ref_c(Xc) @ D.T, Xc.shape[0])]   # MFCC = log-mel -> DCT
+        trials = {}
+        for name, fn, nframes in cells:
+            t = timing.bench_trials(fn, sync)                       # per-trial distribution
+            trials[name] = t
+            import numpy as _np
+            rows.append([platform_id, name, secs, nframes, float(_np.median(t)),
+                         float(_np.percentile(t, 25)), float(_np.percentile(t, 75))])
+        # bootstrap CI on each speedup ratio (baseline-latency / proposed-latency)
+        for pair, base, prop in (("melt_vs_stft", "stft_mel", "melt"),
+                                 ("mfcct_vs_mfcc", "mfcc", "mfcct")):
+            r = stats.bootstrap_ratio_ci(trials[base], trials[prop])
+            spd.append([platform_id, secs, pair, r["ratio"], r["lo"], r["hi"]])
+
+    io.write_csv(csv, ["platform", "frontend", "secs", "frames",
+                       "median_ms", "p25_ms", "p75_ms"], rows)
+    io.write_csv(out / "speedup.csv",
+                 ["platform", "secs", "pair", "speedup", "ci_lo", "ci_hi"], spd)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "latency", platform_id, "configs/experiments/latency.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv} + speedup.csv")

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/mlx_bench.py — MLX-backend latency/energy: MelT vs STFT+Mel (Apple)
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Tier-2: puts ACTUAL numbers behind the paper's note that the STFT+Mel baseline
+# runs faster under Apple's MLX than under MPS, so the M4 Pro speedup cannot be
+# read as MPS-vs-best-baseline cherry-picking. Pure MLX (no torch): MelT is one
+# matmul; the baseline uses mlx.core.fft. Energy via integrated powermetrics
+# (GPU-only, same method as the Apple rows of Table IV). Writes mlx.csv.
+# NOTE: requires `mlx` on Apple Silicon; cannot run on CUDA/Linux.
+# =============================================================================
+"""MLX-backend MelT vs STFT+Mel (latency + integrated-powermetrics energy)."""
+import math
+import numpy as np
+from melt import timing, io, power
+from . import _common as C
+
+EPS = 1e-6
+
+
+class _MpsShim:
+    """Minimal device shim so power.measure_energy_stats takes the Apple path
+    without importing torch (MLX runs on the same GPU)."""
+    type = "mps"
+
+
+def _hz_to_mel(f):  return 2595.0 * math.log10(1.0 + f / 700.0)
+def _mel_to_hz(m):  return 700.0 * (10.0 ** (m / 2595.0) - 1.0)
+
+
+def _hann(n_win):
+    n = np.arange(n_win, dtype=np.float64)
+    return (0.5 - 0.5 * np.cos(2.0 * math.pi * n / (n_win - 1))).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def _frames(audio, frame_len, hop):
+    audio = np.asarray(audio, np.float32)
+    nf = max(1, (len(audio) - frame_len) // hop + 1)
+    idx = np.arange(frame_len)[None, :] + hop * np.arange(nf)[:, None]
+    return audio[idx].astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def _meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max):
+    mel_pts = np.linspace(_hz_to_mel(f_min), _hz_to_mel(f_max), n_mels + 2)[1:-1]
+    freqs = np.array([_mel_to_hz(m) for m in mel_pts], dtype=np.float64)
+    n = np.arange(frame_len, dtype=np.float64)
+    win = _hann(frame_len)
+    phase = 2.0 * math.pi * np.outer(freqs, n) / sr
+    return ((np.cos(phase) * win).astype(np.float32),
+            (np.sin(phase) * win).astype(np.float32))
+
+
+def _mel_filterbank(n_mels, n_freqs, sr, f_min, f_max):
+    mel_pts = np.linspace(_hz_to_mel(f_min), _hz_to_mel(f_max), n_mels + 2)
+    hz_pts = np.array([_mel_to_hz(m) for m in mel_pts])
+    fbin = hz_pts / (sr / 2) * (n_freqs - 1)
+    fb = np.zeros((n_mels, n_freqs), dtype=np.float32)
+    for j in range(1, n_mels + 1):
+        lo, ctr, hi = fbin[j - 1], fbin[j], fbin[j + 1]
+        for k in range(n_freqs):
+            if lo < k < ctr:    fb[j - 1, k] = (k - lo) / (ctr - lo)
+            elif ctr <= k < hi: fb[j - 1, k] = (hi - k) / (hi - ctr)
+    return fb
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import mlx.core as mx
+    cfg = C.load_config("energy"); dev_str = C.platform_device(platform_id)
+    if dev_str != "mps":
+        print(f"  skip mlx: {platform_id} is not Apple Silicon"); return
+    out = io.out_dir(platform_id); csv = out / "mlx.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+
+    sp = cfg["spectral"]; sr = cfg["sr"]; dur = cfg["energy"]["duration_s"]
+    N, H, n_mels = sp["frame_len"], sp["hop_len"], sp["n_mels"]
+    audio = C.load_audio(cfg, dur)
+
+    X_np = _frames(audio, N, H)
+    w_r, w_i = _meltf_weights(n_mels, N, sr, sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"])
+    win = _hann(N)
+    fb = _mel_filterbank(n_mels, N // 2 + 1, sr, sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"])
+
+    X = mx.array(X_np)
+    WrT, WiT = mx.array(w_r.T.copy()), mx.array(w_i.T.copy())
+    winx, fbT = mx.array(win), mx.array(fb.T.copy())
+
+    def melt():       # one matmul pair, no FFT
+        return mx.log((X @ WrT) ** 2 + (X @ WiT) ** 2 + EPS)
+
+    def stft_mel():   # conventional: rfft -> power -> Mel filterbank
+        spec = mx.fft.rfft(X * winx)
+        return mx.log((mx.abs(spec) ** 2) @ fbT + EPS)
+
+    dev = _MpsShim()
+    sync = lambda: None                         # MLX sync is mx.eval(...) below
+    ecfg = cfg["energy"]
+    rows = []
+    for name, fn in (("melt", melt), ("stft_mel", stft_mel)):
+        f = (lambda fn=fn: mx.eval(fn()))       # force MLX evaluation per call
+        lat = timing.bench(f, sync)[0]
+        r = power.measure_energy_stats(f, sync, dev, lat,
+                                       window_s=ecfg["power_window_s"],
+                                       period_ms=ecfg["nvml_period_ms"],
+                                       n_trials=ecfg.get("n_energy_trials", 10))
+        rows.append([platform_id, name, lat, r["power_w"], r["energy_measured_mj"],
+                     r["n_calls_window"], r["window_s_actual"], "mlx+" + r["method"]])
+    io.write_csv(csv, ["platform", "frontend", "latency_ms", "power_w",
+                       "energy_measured_mj", "n_calls_window", "window_s_actual",
+                       "method"], rows)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "mlx", platform_id, "configs/experiments/energy.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}")

+# =============================================================================
+"""Mel-bin sweep: speedup = STFT+Mel / MelT at M in {40,80,128,256,512}."""

+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
