+
+def file_sha256_12(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as f:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()[:12]
+
+
+def machine_id() -> str:
+    return f"{slug(socket.gethostname())}_{slug(platform.platform())}"
+
+
+def progress(xs: Iterable, desc: str):
+    return tqdm(xs, desc=desc, leave=False) if tqdm is not None else xs
+
+
+def setup_device(requested: str | None) -> torch.device:
+    if requested:
+        return torch.device(requested)
+    if torch.cuda.is_available():
+        torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True
+        torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True
+        return torch.device("cuda")
+    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
+        return torch.device("mps")
+    return torch.device("cpu")
+
+
+def read_audio(path: Path) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    try:
+        x, sr = sf.read(str(path), dtype="float32", always_2d=False)
+        if x.ndim > 1:
+            x = x.mean(axis=1)
+        if sr != SR:
+            old = np.arange(len(x), dtype=np.float64)
+            new_len = max(1, int(round(len(x) * SR / sr)))
+            new = np.linspace(0, max(0, len(x) - 1), new_len, dtype=np.float64)
+            x = np.interp(new, old, x).astype(np.float32)
+        return x.astype(np.float32, copy=False)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+# ----------------------------- dataset loading -------------------------------
+def load_folder_dataset(root: Path, max_per_class: int | None) -> list[Item]:
+    class_dirs = sorted([p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()])
+    if not class_dirs:
+        raise SystemExit(f"No class folders found in {root}")
+
+    items: list[Item] = []
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
+    for cls in class_dirs:
+        files = sorted([p for p in cls.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS])
+        if max_per_class is not None and len(files) > max_per_class:
+            files = sorted(rng.choice(files, size=max_per_class, replace=False).tolist())
+        items.extend(Item(path=p, label=cls.name, group=None) for p in files)
+    return items
+
+
+def first_existing(row: dict, names: list[str]) -> str | None:
+    for name in names:
+        if name in row and str(row[name]).strip():
+            return str(row[name]).strip()
+    return None
+
+
+def load_manifest_dataset(manifest: Path, root: Path, label_col: str, group_col: str | None,
+                          max_per_class: int | None) -> list[Item]:
+    with manifest.open(newline="") as f:
+        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+    if not rows:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Empty manifest: {manifest}")
+    if label_col not in rows[0]:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Label column {label_col!r} not found. Columns: {list(rows[0].keys())}")
+    if group_col and group_col not in rows[0]:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Group column {group_col!r} not found. Columns: {list(rows[0].keys())}")
+
+    tmp: list[Item] = []
+    for r in rows:
+        rel = first_existing(r, ["path", "filepath", "file", "filename", "relative_path", "audio"])
+        if rel is None:
+            raise SystemExit("Manifest needs a path column: path/filepath/file/filename/relative_path/audio")
+        p = Path(rel)
+        if not p.is_absolute():
+            p = root / p
+        tmp.append(Item(path=p, label=str(r[label_col]), group=str(r[group_col]) if group_col else None))
+
+    if max_per_class is None:
+        return tmp
+
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
+    out: list[Item] = []
+    for label in sorted(set(i.label for i in tmp)):
+        cls_items = [i for i in tmp if i.label == label]
+        if len(cls_items) > max_per_class:
+            idx = rng.choice(np.arange(len(cls_items)), size=max_per_class, replace=False)
+            cls_items = [cls_items[int(j)] for j in idx]
+        out.extend(cls_items)
+    return out
+
+
+def split_items(items: list[Item], test_size: float, seed: int, group_disjoint: bool) -> tuple[list[Item], list[Item], str]:
+    y = np.array([i.label for i in items])
+
+    if group_disjoint:
+        groups = np.array([i.group for i in items])
+        if any(g is None or g == "" for g in groups):
+            raise SystemExit("--group-disjoint requires every item to have a non-empty group.")
+        # One split from StratifiedGroupKFold; choose n_splits close to 1/test_size.
+        n_splits = max(2, int(round(1.0 / test_size)))
+        sgkf = StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=n_splits, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)
+        train_idx, test_idx = next(sgkf.split(np.zeros(len(items)), y, groups))
+        mode = f"StratifiedGroupKFold speaker/group-disjoint, n_splits={n_splits}"
+    else:
+        idx = np.arange(len(items))
+        train_idx, test_idx = train_test_split(idx, test_size=test_size, random_state=seed, stratify=y)
+        mode = f"StratifiedShuffleSplit file-level, test_size={test_size}"
+
+    return [items[int(i)] for i in train_idx], [items[int(i)] for i in test_idx], mode
+
+
+def load_explicit_test(train_root: Path, test_root: Path, max_per_class: int | None) -> tuple[list[Item], list[Item], str]:
+    train = load_folder_dataset(train_root, max_per_class)
+    test_raw = load_folder_dataset(test_root, max_per_class)
+    train_labels = sorted(set(i.label for i in train))
+    test = [i for i in test_raw if i.label in train_labels]
+    skipped = len(test_raw) - len(test)
+    mode = "explicit train/test folders"
+    if skipped:
+        mode += f"; skipped {skipped} test files with labels absent from train"
+    return train, test, mode
+
+
+# ----------------------------- frontend math --------------------------------
+def hz_to_mel(hz: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float:
+    return 2595.0 * np.log10(1.0 + np.asarray(hz) / 700.0)
+
+
+def mel_to_hz(mel: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float:
+    return 700.0 * (10.0 ** (np.asarray(mel) / 2595.0) - 1.0)
+
+
+def hann(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    k = np.arange(n)
+    return (0.5 - 0.5 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * k / (n - 1))).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def build_mel_filterbank() -> torch.Tensor:
+    fft_f = np.linspace(0.0, SR / 2.0, N_FREQS)
+    mel_pts = np.linspace(hz_to_mel(F_MIN), hz_to_mel(F_MAX), N_MELS + 2)
+    hz_pts = mel_to_hz(mel_pts)
+    fb = np.zeros((N_MELS, N_FREQS), dtype=np.float32)
+    for m in range(1, N_MELS + 1):
+        fl, fc, fr = hz_pts[m - 1], hz_pts[m], hz_pts[m + 1]
+        left = (fft_f - fl) / (fc - fl + 1e-12)
+        right = (fr - fft_f) / (fr - fc + 1e-12)
+        fb[m - 1] = np.maximum(0.0, np.minimum(left, right))
+    return torch.from_numpy(fb)
+
+
+def build_meltf_weights() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    # MelT projection bases from the single canonical kernel (same [1:-1] Mel-
+    # center grid + symmetric Hann this file used before; W_i sign differs but is
+    # irrelevant, since fe_meltf uses W_r^2 + W_i^2).
+    wr, wi = _dsp.meltf_weights(N_MELS, FRAME_LEN, SR, F_MIN, F_MAX)
+    return torch.from_numpy(wr), torch.from_numpy(wi)
+
+
+def build_dct_matrix() -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Orthonormal DCT-II from the canonical kernel (shared by MFCC and MFCCT).
+    return torch.from_numpy(_dsp.dct_ii_matrix(N_MFCC, N_MELS))
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Weights:
+    window: torch.Tensor
+    W_mel: torch.Tensor
+    W_r: torch.Tensor
+    W_i: torch.Tensor
+    D: torch.Tensor
+
+    def to(self, device: torch.device) -> "Weights":
+        return Weights(self.window.to(device), self.W_mel.to(device), self.W_r.to(device), self.W_i.to(device), self.D.to(device))
+
+
+def build_weights(device: torch.device) -> Weights:
+    wr, wi = build_meltf_weights()
+    return Weights(
+        window=torch.from_numpy(hann(FRAME_LEN)),
+        W_mel=build_mel_filterbank(),
+        W_r=wr,
+        W_i=wi,
+        D=build_dct_matrix(),
+    ).to(device)
+
+
+def fe_stft_mel(X: torch.Tensor, w: Weights) -> torch.Tensor:
+    spec = torch.fft.rfft(X * w.window, n=N_FFT)
+    power = spec.real.square() + spec.imag.square()
+    return power @ w.W_mel.T
+
+
+def fe_mfcc(X: torch.Tensor, w: Weights) -> torch.Tensor:
+    mel = fe_stft_mel(X, w)
+    return torch.log(mel + EPS) @ w.D.T
+
+
+def fe_meltf(X: torch.Tensor, w: Weights) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # MelT energy projection from the canonical kernel (S = |X W_r^T|^2 + |X W_i^T|^2),
+    # evaluated as one fused GEMM against the stacked basis [W_r; W_i].
+    return _project(X, torch.cat([w.W_r, w.W_i], dim=0), w.W_r.shape[0])
+
+
+def fe_mfcct(X: torch.Tensor, w: Weights) -> torch.Tensor:
+    mel = fe_meltf(X, w)
+    return torch.log(mel + EPS) @ w.D.T
+
+
+def frontend_pair(pair: str) -> tuple[str, Callable[[torch.Tensor, Weights], torch.Tensor], str, Callable[[torch.Tensor, Weights], torch.Tensor]]:
+    if pair == "mfcc_mfcct":
+        return "MFCC", fe_mfcc, "MFCCT", fe_mfcct
+    if pair == "mel_meltf":
+        return "STFT+Mel", fe_stft_mel, "MelTF", fe_meltf
+    raise SystemExit(f"Unknown --pair {pair!r}")
+
+
+# ----------------------------- feature extraction ----------------------------
+def frame_audio(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    if len(x) < FRAME_LEN:
+        x = np.pad(x, (0, FRAME_LEN - len(x)))
+    starts = np.arange(0, len(x) - FRAME_LEN + 1, HOP_LEN)
+    if len(starts) == 0:
+        starts = np.array([0])
+    return np.stack([x[s:s + FRAME_LEN] for s in starts]).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def extract_one(path: Path, fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor, Weights], torch.Tensor], weights: Weights,
+                device: torch.device) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    x = read_audio(path)
+    if x is None:
+        return None
+    frames = frame_audio(x)
+    X = torch.from_numpy(frames).to(device)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        Y = fn(X, weights).detach().cpu().numpy()
+    # Intentionally simple, identical pooling for both frontends.
+    return np.concatenate([Y.mean(axis=0), Y.std(axis=0)]).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def extract_matrix(items: list[Item], fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor, Weights], torch.Tensor], weights: Weights,
+                   device: torch.device, name: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[int]]:
+    X: list[np.ndarray] = []
+    kept: list[int] = []
+    for idx, item in enumerate(progress(items, f"extract {name}")):
+        feat = extract_one(item.path, fn, weights, device)
+        if feat is not None and np.all(np.isfinite(feat)):
+            X.append(feat)
+            kept.append(idx)
+    if not X:
+        raise SystemExit(f"No valid audio/features for {name}")
+    return np.stack(X), kept
+
+
+def align_two(X1: np.ndarray, k1: list[int], X2: np.ndarray, k2: list[int], items: list[Item]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list[Item]]:
+    d1 = {idx: row for row, idx in zip(X1, k1)}
+    d2 = {idx: row for row, idx in zip(X2, k2)}
+    common = sorted(set(d1) & set(d2))
+    return np.stack([d1[i] for i in common]), np.stack([d2[i] for i in common]), [items[i] for i in common]
+
+
+# ----------------------------- modeling/statistics ---------------------------
+def make_estimator(seed: int, max_iter: int) -> Pipeline:
+    # Same classifier for both representations. class_weight handles imbalance fairly.
+    clf = LogisticRegression(
+        solver="lbfgs",
+        max_iter=max_iter,
+        class_weight="balanced",
+        random_state=seed,
+        n_jobs=None,
+    )
+    return Pipeline([
+        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
+        ("clf", clf),
+    ])
+
+
+def fit_with_inner_cv(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, groups: np.ndarray | None, seed: int,
+                      max_iter: int, inner_folds: int) -> tuple[Pipeline, dict]:
+    n_classes = len(np.unique(y))
+    min_class = min(np.bincount(y))
+    folds = max(2, min(inner_folds, int(min_class)))
+    estimator = make_estimator(seed, max_iter)
+    grid = {"clf__C": [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0]}
+
+    if groups is not None and len(set(groups.tolist())) >= folds:
+        cv = StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=folds, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)
+        search = GridSearchCV(estimator, grid, scoring="f1_macro", cv=cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True)
+        search.fit(X, y, groups=groups)
+    else:
+        cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=folds, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)
+        search = GridSearchCV(estimator, grid, scoring="f1_macro", cv=cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True)
+        search.fit(X, y)
+
+    return search.best_estimator_, {"best_C": search.best_params_["clf__C"], "inner_cv_f1_macro": float(search.best_score_), "inner_folds": folds}
+
+
+def mcnemar(y_true: np.ndarray, pred_a: np.ndarray, pred_b: np.ndarray) -> dict:
+    a_ok = pred_a == y_true
+    b_ok = pred_b == y_true
+    b01 = int(np.sum(a_ok & ~b_ok))  # A correct, B wrong
+    b10 = int(np.sum(~a_ok & b_ok))  # A wrong, B correct
+    n = b01 + b10
+    if n == 0:
+        return {"b01_a_only": b01, "b10_b_only": b10, "chi2": 0.0, "p": 1.0}
+    stat = (abs(b01 - b10) - 1) ** 2 / n  # continuity-corrected
+    p = float(chi2.sf(stat, 1)) if chi2 is not None else float("nan")
+    return {"b01_a_only": b01, "b10_b_only": b10, "chi2": float(stat), "p": p}
+
+
+def bootstrap_delta_ci(y_true: np.ndarray, pred_a: np.ndarray, pred_b: np.ndarray,
+                       n_boot: int, seed: int) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    n = len(y_true)
+    deltas = np.empty(n_boot, dtype=np.float64)
+    for i in range(n_boot):
+        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
+        acc_a = accuracy_score(y_true[idx], pred_a[idx])
+        acc_b = accuracy_score(y_true[idx], pred_b[idx])
+        deltas[i] = acc_b - acc_a
+    return float(np.mean(deltas)), float(np.percentile(deltas, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(deltas, 97.5))
+
+
+def evaluate(name: str, model: Pipeline, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> dict:
+    pred = model.predict(X)
+    return {
+        "name": name,
+        "pred": pred,
+        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y, pred)),
+        "f1_macro": float(f1_score(y, pred, average="macro")),
+    }
+
+
+# ----------------------------- reporting ------------------------------------
+def write_csv_row(path: Path, row: dict) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with path.open("w", newline="") as f:
+        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(row.keys()))
+        w.writeheader()
+        w.writerow(row)
+
+
+def write_report(path: Path, lines: list[str]) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+
+def class_distribution(items: list[Item]) -> str:
+    labels = sorted(set(i.label for i in items))
+    return ", ".join(f"{lab}={sum(i.label == lab for i in items)}" for lab in labels)
+
+
+# ----------------------------- main -----------------------------------------
+def main() -> None:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fair paired comparison of two audio frontends.")
+    src = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
+    src.add_argument("--corpus-path", type=Path, help="class-per-folder dataset root")
+    src.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, help="CSV manifest")
+    ap.add_argument("--manifest-root", type=Path, default=None)
+    ap.add_argument("--label-col", default="label")
+    ap.add_argument("--group-col", default=None, help="speaker/group column for leakage-safe split/CV")
+    ap.add_argument("--group-disjoint", action="store_true", help="make train/test split group-disjoint")
+    ap.add_argument("--test-path", type=Path, default=None, help="explicit class-per-folder test root; only with --corpus-path")
+    ap.add_argument("--pair", choices=["mfcc_mfcct", "mel_meltf"], default="mfcc_mfcct")
+    ap.add_argument("--dataset-name", default=None)
+    ap.add_argument("--test-size", type=float, default=0.2)
+    ap.add_argument("--max-per-class", type=int, default=None)
+    ap.add_argument("--device", default=None)
+    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=SEED)
+    ap.add_argument("--inner-folds", type=int, default=5)
+    ap.add_argument("--max-iter", type=int, default=2000)
+    ap.add_argument("--bootstrap", type=int, default=2000)
+    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="results",
+                    help="where to write <dataset>_<pair>_fair.{csv,txt}")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    seed_everything(args.seed)
+    device = setup_device(args.device)
+    left_name, left_fn, right_name, right_fn = frontend_pair(args.pair)
+
+    if args.corpus_path and args.test_path:
+        train_items, test_items, split_mode = load_explicit_test(args.corpus_path, args.test_path, args.max_per_class)
+    elif args.corpus_path:
+        items = load_folder_dataset(args.corpus_path, args.max_per_class)
+        train_items, test_items, split_mode = split_items(items, args.test_size, args.seed, group_disjoint=False)
+    else:
+        root = args.manifest_root or args.manifest.parent
+        items = load_manifest_dataset(args.manifest, root, args.label_col, args.group_col, args.max_per_class)
+        train_items, test_items, split_mode = split_items(items, args.test_size, args.seed, args.group_disjoint)
+
+    dataset_name = args.dataset_name or (args.manifest.stem if args.manifest else args.corpus_path.name)
+
+    print(f"\n[classify_fair] {left_name} vs {right_name}")
+    print(f"  dataset : {dataset_name}")
+    print(f"  device  : {device}")
+    print(f"  split   : {split_mode}")
+    print(f"  train   : {len(train_items)} files | {class_distribution(train_items)}")
+    print(f"  test    : {len(test_items)} files | {class_distribution(test_items)}")
+
+    # Encode labels using train labels only; reject unknown test labels.
+    le = LabelEncoder()
+    y_train_all = le.fit_transform([i.label for i in train_items])
+    valid_test_mask = np.array([i.label in set(le.classes_) for i in test_items])
+    if not valid_test_mask.all():
+        dropped = int(np.sum(~valid_test_mask))
+        print(f"  [warn] dropped {dropped} test items with labels absent from train")
+        test_items = [i for i, keep in zip(test_items, valid_test_mask) if keep]
+    y_test_all = le.transform([i.label for i in test_items])
+
+    train_groups = None
+    if args.group_col and all(i.group is not None for i in train_items):
+        train_groups = np.array([i.group for i in train_items])
+
+    weights = build_weights(device)
+
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    XL_tr_raw, keep_l_tr = extract_matrix(train_items, left_fn, weights, device, f"{left_name} train")
+    XR_tr_raw, keep_r_tr = extract_matrix(train_items, right_fn, weights, device, f"{right_name} train")
+    XL_te_raw, keep_l_te = extract_matrix(test_items, left_fn, weights, device, f"{left_name} test")
+    XR_te_raw, keep_r_te = extract_matrix(test_items, right_fn, weights, device, f"{right_name} test")
+    extract_s = time.perf_counter() - t0
+
+    XL_tr, XR_tr, train_kept_items = align_two(XL_tr_raw, keep_l_tr, XR_tr_raw, keep_r_tr, train_items)
+    XL_te, XR_te, test_kept_items = align_two(XL_te_raw, keep_l_te, XR_te_raw, keep_r_te, test_items)
+    y_train = le.transform([i.label for i in train_kept_items])
+    y_test = le.transform([i.label for i in test_kept_items])
+    groups_kept = None
+    if train_groups is not None:
+        groups_kept = np.array([i.group for i in train_kept_items])
+
+    print(f"  aligned : train={len(y_train)} test={len(y_test)}")
+    print(f"  dims    : {left_name}={XL_tr.shape[1]} {right_name}={XR_tr.shape[1]}")
+
+    left_model, left_cv = fit_with_inner_cv(XL_tr, y_train, groups_kept, args.seed, args.max_iter, args.inner_folds)
+    right_model, right_cv = fit_with_inner_cv(XR_tr, y_train, groups_kept, args.seed, args.max_iter, args.inner_folds)
+
+    left_eval = evaluate(left_name, left_model, XL_te, y_test)
+    right_eval = evaluate(right_name, right_model, XR_te, y_test)
+    # Drop-in / cross-frontend (forward only): apply the LEFT (baseline) trained
+    # pipeline to the RIGHT (proposed) test features — e.g. train MFCC, test MFCCT
+    # with NO retraining. This is the VoxCeleb analogue of the frozen-Whisper swap;
+    # accuracy near the left same-frontend baseline ⇒ the proposed front end is a
+    # drop-in. Dims match by design (MFCC/MFCCT 26, STFT+Mel/MelT 160).
+    cross_eval = (evaluate(f"{left_name}->{right_name}", left_model, XR_te, y_test)
+                  if XR_te.shape[1] == XL_tr.shape[1] else None)
+    mc = mcnemar(y_test, left_eval["pred"], right_eval["pred"])
+    delta_mean, delta_lo, delta_hi = bootstrap_delta_ci(
+        y_test, left_eval["pred"], right_eval["pred"], args.bootstrap, args.seed

+# =============================================================================
+# tasks/whisper.py — frozen-Whisper drop-in equivalence -> Table IX, Fig 6
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# CUDA-only; the result (WER) is hardware-independent. We swap Whisper's log-Mel
+# front end for a Whisper-matched MelT front end, keep the weights FROZEN, decode
+# greedily (so dWER isolates the front end), evaluate the full LibriSpeech
+# test-clean, then run a per-speaker TOST on dWER at +/-1 and +/-2 pp margins.
+#
+# Ported and cleaned from:
+#   exp/meltf/meltf-exp-05-whisper/melt-exp-05-whisper-eval.py  (eval loop)
+#   exp/meltf/meltf-exp-05-whisper/whisper_tost.py              (per-speaker TOST)
+# The MelT front end below is the *Whisper-matched* variant: it reuses the single
+# canonical MelT kernel from src/melt (dsp.meltf_weights + melt.direct_mel_projection)
+# and only adds Whisper-specific wrapping — reflect-pad framing and Whisper's log10
+# normalisation. Its feature cosine to Whisper's native mel is ~0.84 (the deliberate
+# front-end mismatch that makes the task-level equivalence result meaningful).
+# Output: results/raw/tasks/.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Frozen-Whisper front-end swap + per-speaker TOST on dWER (full test-clean)."""
+import re
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+from melt import stats, io, dsp
+from melt.melt import direct_mel_projection
+from .. import _common as C
+
+
+# --- text normalisation (verbatim from the source eval) ----------------------
+def _normalize(s):
+    s = s.lower().strip()
+    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s']", " ", s)
+    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
+
+
+# --- Whisper-matched MelT front end (reflect-pad framing + Whisper log-norm) --
+# Verbatim math from the source script; this is the 0.84-cosine front end.
+def _frame_whisper_style(x, frame_len=400, hop_len=160):
+    import torch
+    pad = frame_len // 2
+    x = torch.nn.functional.pad(x.view(1, 1, -1), (pad, pad), mode="reflect").view(-1)
+    n_frames = 1 + (x.shape[0] - frame_len) // hop_len
+    idx = (torch.arange(frame_len, device=x.device)[None, :]
+           + hop_len * torch.arange(n_frames, device=x.device)[:, None])
+    return x[idx].float()
+
+
+def _whisper_log_normalize(S):
+    import torch
+    log_spec = torch.clamp(S, min=1e-10).log10()
+    log_spec = torch.maximum(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0)
+    return (log_spec + 4.0) / 4.0
+
+
+def melt_logmel_whisper(audio, sr=16000, n_mels=80, frame_len=400, hop_len=160,
+                        f_min=0.0, f_max=8000.0):
+    """MelT log-Mel matched to Whisper's 80-bin spec (single GEMM + Whisper norm).
+
+    The projection bases and the energy GEMM come from the single canonical kernel
+    in src/melt — NOT re-derived here. This front end only adds the Whisper-
+    specific pieces: reflect-pad framing and Whisper's log10 normalisation. The
+    Mel bases (incl. the standard symmetric Hann window) are exactly the repo-wide
+    canonical ones, so MelT lives in one place with no per-experiment variant.
+    """
+    import torch
+    dev = audio.device
+    frames = _frame_whisper_style(audio, frame_len, hop_len).to(torch.float32)
+    w_r, w_i = dsp.meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max)
+    w_r = torch.from_numpy(w_r).to(dev); w_i = torch.from_numpy(w_i).to(dev)
+    w_ri = torch.cat([w_r, w_i], dim=0)                      # stacked basis [2*n_mels, N]
+    S = direct_mel_projection(frames, w_ri, n_mels)          # [T, n_mels], one fused GEMM
+    return _whisper_log_normalize(S.T)
+
+
+def _load_ground_truth(root):
+    """Parse LibriSpeech *.trans.txt -> {utt_id: reference text}."""
+    gt = {}
+    for txt in Path(root).rglob("*.trans.txt"):
+        for line in open(txt):
+            uid, text = line.strip().split(" ", 1)
+            gt[uid] = text
+    return gt
+
+
+def run(platform_id=None, force=False, **_):
+    cfg = C.load_config("whisper")
+    out = io.out_dir(tasks=True); csv = out / "whisper_scaling.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+
+    import torch, whisper
+    from jiwer import wer
+    root = Path(cfg["dataset_root"]) / "librispeech" / "test-clean"
+    files = sorted(root.rglob("*.flac")) + sorted(root.rglob("*.wav"))
+    assert files, f"no test-clean audio under {root} (see data/download_librispeech.sh)"
+    gt = _load_ground_truth(root)
+    dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
+    opts = whisper.DecodingOptions(language="en", without_timestamps=True,
+                                   fp16=(dev == "cuda"))
+
+    rows = []
+    for name in cfg["whisper"]["models"]:
+        model = whisper.load_model(name, device=dev)
+        by_speaker = defaultdict(list)        # speaker -> list of per-utt dWER
+        wer_nat_all, wer_melt_all = [], []
+        for path in files:
+            uid = path.stem
+            ref = gt.get(uid)
+            if ref is None:
+                continue
+            speaker = uid.split("-")[0]
+            audio_np = whisper.pad_or_trim(whisper.load_audio(str(path)))
+            audio = torch.from_numpy(audio_np).to(dev)
+            # native vs MelT log-Mel (MelT trimmed/padded to native's frame count)
+            mel_nat = whisper.log_mel_spectrogram(audio_np, n_mels=80).to(dev)
+            mel_melt = melt_logmel_whisper(audio)[:, :mel_nat.shape[1]]
+            if mel_melt.shape[1] < mel_nat.shape[1]:
+                mel_melt = torch.nn.functional.pad(
+                    mel_melt, (0, mel_nat.shape[1] - mel_melt.shape[1]))
+            r = _normalize(ref)
+            w_nat = wer(r, _normalize(whisper.decode(model, mel_nat, opts).text))
+            w_melt = wer(r, _normalize(whisper.decode(model, mel_melt, opts).text))
+            wer_nat_all.append(w_nat); wer_melt_all.append(w_melt)
+            by_speaker[speaker].append(w_melt - w_nat)
+        # per-speaker dWER (the honest unit for the TOST: utterances cluster by
+        # speaker). The reported mean_dwer_pp, however, is the per-UTTERANCE delta
+        # so it equals (wer_melt - wer_native) of the two columns in this row;
+        # mean_dwer_spk_pp keeps the per-speaker mean for reference.
+        spk_dwer = np.array([np.mean(v) for v in by_speaker.values()])
+        wer_nat_m, wer_melt_m = float(np.mean(wer_nat_all)), float(np.mean(wer_melt_all))
+        row = {"model": name, "n_utt": len(wer_nat_all), "n_speakers": len(spk_dwer),
+               "wer_native": wer_nat_m, "wer_melt": wer_melt_m,
+               "mean_dwer_pp": (wer_melt_m - wer_nat_m) * 100,
+               "mean_dwer_spk_pp": float(spk_dwer.mean() * 100)}
+        for margin_pp in cfg["whisper"]["tost_margins_pp"]:
+            t = stats.tost(spk_dwer, margin_pp / 100.0)   # per-speaker TOST
+            row[f"equiv_{int(margin_pp)}pp"] = int(t["equivalent"])
+            row[f"tost_p_{int(margin_pp)}"] = t["p"]       # raw TOST p (for Holm)
+            row[f"ci90_lo_pp_{int(margin_pp)}"] = round(t["ci90"][0] * 100, 3)
+            row[f"ci90_hi_pp_{int(margin_pp)}"] = round(t["ci90"][1] * 100, 3)
+        rows.append(row)
+        print(f"  {name}: dWER {row['mean_dwer_pp']:+.2f} pp  "
+              f"(n={row['n_utt']}, {row['n_speakers']} spk)")
+
+    # Holm-Bonferroni across the MODELS (family) for each margin, so the
+    # equivalence claims control the family-wise error rate (Tier 1, strong stats).
+    for margin_pp in cfg["whisper"]["tost_margins_pp"]:
+        mk = int(margin_pp)
+        corrected = stats.holm_bonferroni([r[f"tost_p_{mk}"] for r in rows])
+        for r, hc in zip(rows, corrected):
+            r[f"tost_p_{mk}_holm"] = round(hc["p_adj"], 6)
+            r[f"equiv_{mk}pp_holm"] = int(hc["reject"])
+
+    header = list(rows[0].keys())
+    io.write_csv(csv, header, [[r[k] for k in header] for r in rows])
+    io.write_run_json(out, "whisper", platform_id, "configs/experiments/whisper.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}")

+# =============================================================================
+# experiments/v100_power_profile.py — locked-clock power + kernel mix -> Fig 8
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+# Confirms the V100 power inversion is architectural (compute- vs memory-bound),
+# supplying the points for the roofline figure (see melt/roofline.py).
+# Run with the core clock locked first:  sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 1530
+#
+# Measurement protocol (matches the original v100_power_profile.py):
+#   * FP32 forced (TF32 OFF) — the inversion argument requires an honest fp32
+#     measurement; on a true V100 the flag is a no-op, but we keep it explicit so
+#     the script is also correct if run on an Ampere+ GPU.
+#   * GPU kept SATURATED: sync only every `sync_every` calls (not per call) so
+#     CPU launch gaps cannot bias power toward the faster (MelT) frontend.
+#   * MelT and STFT+Mel ALTERNATED over `reps` to cancel thermal drift; we report
+#     the mean power across reps and its across-rep std.
+# =============================================================================
+"""V100 locked-clock power profile feeding the roofline figure."""
+import time
+import numpy as np
+from melt import MelT, timing, io, baselines, power, roofline
+from . import _common as C
+
+SYNC_EVERY = 32   # ~32 kernels in flight: keeps the device saturated during sampling
+
+
+def _saturated_power_w(fn, sync, window_s, period_ms=25):
+    """Median NVML power (W) while `fn` runs back-to-back, syncing every
+    SYNC_EVERY calls so the GPU stays saturated (no per-call launch-gap bias)."""
+    with power.NVMLSampler(period_ms) as s:
+        t0 = time.perf_counter(); n = 0
+        while time.perf_counter() - t0 < window_s:
+            fn(); n += 1
+            if n % SYNC_EVERY == 0:
+                sync()
+        sync()
+        return s.median_w()
+
+
+def run(platform_id, force=False, **_):
+    import torch
+    cfg = C.load_config("v100_power"); out = io.out_dir(platform_id)
+    csv = out / "v100_power.csv"
+    if csv.exists() and not force:
+        print(f"  skip (exists): {csv}"); return
+    # FP32 honest: set up the device but explicitly DISABLE TF32 (overrides the
+    # default timing.setup_torch policy, which enables it for the speedup tables).
+    dev = timing.setup_torch("cuda"); sync = timing.make_sync(dev)
+    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
+    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
+    sp = cfg["spectral"]; audio = C.load_audio(cfg, 160)
+    window_s = cfg["v100_power"]["window_s"]; reps = cfg["v100_power"]["reps"]
+    m = MelT(sr=cfg["sr"], backend="torch", device="cuda", **sp); X = m.frames(audio)
+    ref = baselines.make_reference(sp["n_mels"], sp["frame_len"], cfg["sr"],
+                                   sp["f_min"], sp["f_max"], "torch", "cuda")
+    fronts = [("melt", lambda: m(X), roofline.OPERATOR_AI["melt"]),
+              ("stft_mel", lambda: ref(X), roofline.OPERATOR_AI["stft_mel"])]
+    lat = {name: timing.bench(fn, sync)[0] for name, fn, _ in fronts}
+
+    # Alternate MelT/STFT over reps so thermal drift cancels between frontends.
+    per_rep = {name: [] for name, _, _ in fronts}
+    for _ in range(reps):
+        for name, fn, _ in fronts:
+            per_rep[name].append(_saturated_power_w(fn, sync, window_s))
+
+    rows = []
+    for name, fn, ai in fronts:
+        p_w = float(np.mean(per_rep[name])); p_sd = float(np.std(per_rep[name]))
+        rows.append([name, p_w, p_sd, lat[name], power.energy_mj(p_w, lat[name]),
+                     ai, roofline.attainable_tflops("v100", ai)])
+    io.write_csv(csv, ["frontend", "power_w", "power_std_w", "latency_ms",
+                       "energy_mj", "arith_intensity", "attainable_tflops"], rows)
+    io.write_run_json(out, "v100_power", platform_id, "configs/experiments/v100_power.yaml")
+    print(f"  wrote {csv}  (fp32, {reps} reps x {window_s}s, "
+          f"ridge={roofline.ridge('v100'):.1f} FLOP/byte)")

+// =============================================================================
+// melt_mpsgraph.swift — MelT on Apple, native, no Python / no torch.
+// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Builds the MelT projection (S = R^2 + I^2 ; log) as an MPSGraph and runs it on
+// the GPU through Metal Performance Shaders Graph — the native Apple path, one
+// layer above the metal. This is the EDGE exploration; the cross-platform table
+// in the paper stays on PyTorch for an apples-to-apples comparison.
+//
+// Run on a Mac (Xcode Command Line Tools installed):
+//     swift melt_mpsgraph.swift
+//   (or drop into an Xcode command-line target.)
+//
+// NOTE: untested in this form — API names in MPSGraph occasionally differ by
+// macOS version; the sensitive calls are flagged with  // <-- CHECK.
+// Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+// =============================================================================
+import Foundation
+import Metal
+import MetalPerformanceShaders
+import MetalPerformanceShadersGraph
+
+// --- config (paper spectral config, Table III) -------------------------------
+let SR = 16000, N = 400, M = 80
+let FMIN = 80.0, FMAX = 7600.0
+let EPS: Double = 1e-6
+let secs = 160.0
+let T = Int(secs * Double(SR) / 160.0)          // frames at hop=160
+
+// --- Mel-center windowed cos/sin bases, stacked as WriT = [N, 2M] ------------
+//     columns 0..<M  = Wr^T (cos),   M..<2M = Wi^T (sin)
+func hz2mel(_ f: Double) -> Double { 2595.0 * log10(1.0 + f / 700.0) }
+func mel2hz(_ m: Double) -> Double { 700.0 * (pow(10.0, m / 2595.0) - 1.0) }
+
+func buildWriT() -> [Float] {
+    let lo = hz2mel(FMIN), hi = hz2mel(FMAX)
+    var freqs = [Double](repeating: 0, count: M)
+    for m in 0..<M { freqs[m] = mel2hz(lo + (hi - lo) * Double(m + 1) / Double(M + 1)) }
+    var win = [Double](repeating: 0, count: N)
+    for n in 0..<N { win[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2.0 * Double.pi * Double(n) / Double(N - 1)) }
+    var w = [Float](repeating: 0, count: N * 2 * M)
+    for n in 0..<N {
+        for m in 0..<M {
+            let ph = 2.0 * Double.pi * freqs[m] * Double(n) / Double(SR)
+            w[n * 2 * M + m]     = Float(cos(ph) * win[n])   // Wr^T
+            w[n * 2 * M + M + m] = Float(sin(ph) * win[n])   // Wi^T
+        }
+    }
+    return w
+}
+
+// --- Metal + buffers ---------------------------------------------------------
+guard let device = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice() else { fatalError("no Metal device") }
+let xData = (0..<(T * N)).map { _ in Float.random(in: -1...1) }
+let wData = buildWriT()
+let fsz = MemoryLayout<Float>.size
+let xBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: xData, length: T * N * fsz, options: .storageModeShared)!
+let wBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: wData, length: wData.count * fsz, options: .storageModeShared)!
+
+// --- MPSGraph: RI = X · WriT ; R,I = halves ; S = R^2+I^2 ; MelT = log(S+eps) -
+let graph = MPSGraph()
+let x    = graph.placeholder(shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: .float32, name: "x")
+let wriT = graph.placeholder(shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: .float32, name: "wriT")
+
+let ri = graph.matrixMultiplication(primary: x, secondary: wriT, name: "proj")     // [T, 2M]
+let r  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: 0, length: M, name: "r")        // <-- CHECK
+let i  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: M, length: M, name: "i")        // <-- CHECK
+let s  = graph.addition(graph.square(with: r, name: "r2"),
+                        graph.square(with: i, name: "i2"), name: "s")
+let eps  = graph.constant(EPS, dataType: .float32)                                  // <-- CHECK
+let melt = graph.logarithm(with: graph.addition(s, eps, name: "seps"), name: "melt")
+
+let feeds: [MPSGraphTensor: MPSGraphTensorData] = [
+    x:    MPSGraphTensorData(xBuf, shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: .float32),
+    wriT: MPSGraphTensorData(wBuf, shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: .float32),
+]
+
+// --- warmup + timed runs (graph.run is synchronous) --------------------------
+func once() { _ = graph.run(feeds: feeds, targetTensors: [melt], targetOperations: nil) }
+for _ in 0..<30 { once() }
+var ts = [Double]()
+for _ in 0..<100 {

+// =============================================================================
+// melt_mpsgraph_exec.swift — MelT on Apple, native, "close to the metal".
+// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Compiles the MelT graph ONCE to an MPSGraphExecutable (no per-call graph
+// construction) and times it two ways:
+//   (A) executable.run() in a loop  -> realistic deployment latency (host+GPU)
+//   (B) GPU-only time via command-buffer timestamps (gpuEndTime - gpuStartTime)
+//       -> the pure Metal kernel time, no host/submission overhead.
+// No Python, no torch. This is the EDGE exploration; the cross-platform paper
+// table stays on PyTorch for an apples-to-apples comparison.
+//
+// Run on a Mac (Xcode CLT):   swift melt_mpsgraph_exec.swift
+// NOTE: untested here (no Swift/Metal in my sandbox). MPSGraph API names shift a
+// bit across macOS versions — sensitive calls flagged  // <-- CHECK.
+// Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+// =============================================================================
+import Foundation
+import Metal
+import MetalPerformanceShaders
+import MetalPerformanceShadersGraph
+
+let SR = 16000, N = 400, M = 80
+let FMIN = 80.0, FMAX = 7600.0
+let EPS: Double = 1e-6
+let secs = 160.0
+let T = Int(secs * Double(SR) / 160.0)
+
+// --- bases: WriT = [N, 2M], cols 0..<M = Wr^T (cos), M..<2M = Wi^T (sin) ------
+func hz2mel(_ f: Double) -> Double { 2595.0 * log10(1.0 + f / 700.0) }
+func mel2hz(_ m: Double) -> Double { 700.0 * (pow(10.0, m / 2595.0) - 1.0) }
+func buildWriT() -> [Float] {
+    let lo = hz2mel(FMIN), hi = hz2mel(FMAX)
+    var freqs = [Double](repeating: 0, count: M)
+    for m in 0..<M { freqs[m] = mel2hz(lo + (hi - lo) * Double(m + 1) / Double(M + 1)) }
+    var win = [Double](repeating: 0, count: N)
+    for n in 0..<N { win[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2.0 * Double.pi * Double(n) / Double(N - 1)) }
+    var w = [Float](repeating: 0, count: N * 2 * M)
+    for n in 0..<N { for m in 0..<M {
+        let ph = 2.0 * Double.pi * freqs[m] * Double(n) / Double(SR)
+        w[n * 2 * M + m]     = Float(cos(ph) * win[n])
+        w[n * 2 * M + M + m] = Float(sin(ph) * win[n])
+    } }
+    return w
+}
+
+// --- Metal + buffers ---------------------------------------------------------
+guard let device = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice() else { fatalError("no Metal device") }
+let queue = device.makeCommandQueue()!
+let fsz = MemoryLayout<Float>.size
+let xData = (0..<(T * N)).map { _ in Float.random(in: -1...1) }
+let wData = buildWriT()
+let xBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: xData, length: T * N * fsz, options: .storageModeShared)!
+let wBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: wData, length: wData.count * fsz, options: .storageModeShared)!
+
+// --- graph: RI = X·WriT ; R,I halves ; S = R^2+I^2 ; MelT = log(S+eps) --------
+let graph = MPSGraph()
+let x    = graph.placeholder(shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: .float32, name: "x")
+let wriT = graph.placeholder(shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: .float32, name: "wriT")
+let ri = graph.matrixMultiplication(primary: x, secondary: wriT, name: "proj")
+let r  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: 0, length: M, name: "r")     // <-- CHECK
+let i  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: M, length: M, name: "i")     // <-- CHECK
+let s  = graph.addition(graph.square(with: r, name: "r2"),
+                        graph.square(with: i, name: "i2"), name: "s")
+let eps  = graph.constant(EPS, dataType: .float32)                               // <-- CHECK
+let melt = graph.logarithm(with: graph.addition(s, eps, name: "seps"), name: "melt")
+
+// --- compile ONCE to an executable ------------------------------------------
+let mpsDevice = MPSGraphDevice(mtlDevice: device)
+let xST = MPSGraphShapedType(shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: .float32)
+let wST = MPSGraphShapedType(shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: .float32)
+let exe = graph.compile(with: mpsDevice,
+                        feeds: [x: xST, wriT: wST],
+                        targetTensors: [melt], targetOperations: nil,
+                        compilationDescriptor: MPSGraphCompilationDescriptor())   // <-- CHECK
+
+let xTD = MPSGraphTensorData(xBuf, shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: .float32)
+let wTD = MPSGraphTensorData(wBuf, shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: .float32)
+// inputs in the executable's feed order
+let byTensor: [MPSGraphTensor: MPSGraphTensorData] = [x: xTD, wriT: wTD]
+let inputs = (exe.feedTensors ?? [x, wriT]).map { byTensor[$0]! }                 // <-- CHECK
+
+func median(_ a: [Double]) -> Double { let s = a.sorted(); return s[s.count / 2] }
+func mn(_ a: [Double]) -> Double { a.min() ?? 0 }
+
+// --- (A) executable.run() loop : realistic deployment latency ---------------
+let runDesc = MPSGraphExecutableExecutionDescriptor()
+runDesc.waitUntilCompleted = true
+for _ in 0..<30 { _ = exe.run(with: queue, inputs: inputs, results: nil, executionDescriptor: runDesc) }
+var ra = [Double]()
+for _ in 0..<100 {
+    let t0 = DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds
+    _ = exe.run(with: queue, inputs: inputs, results: nil, executionDescriptor: runDesc)
+    ra.append(Double(DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds - t0) / 1e6)
+}
+
+// --- (B) pure GPU time : command-buffer timestamps --------------------------
+var gp = [Double]()
+for k in 0..<130 {
+    let cb = queue.makeCommandBuffer()!
+    let mpscb = MPSCommandBuffer(commandBuffer: cb)
+    _ = exe.encode(to: mpscb, inputs: inputs, results: nil, executionDescriptor: nil)  // <-- CHECK
+    mpscb.commit()
+    cb.waitUntilCompleted()
+    if k >= 30 { gp.append((cb.gpuEndTime - cb.gpuStartTime) * 1000.0) }   // s -> ms
+}
+
+print(String(format: "MPSGraph MelT (native)  X[%d,%d] M=%d (~%.0fs)", T, N, M, secs))
+print(String(format: "  (A) executable.run  : median %.4f ms   min %.4f ms   (host+GPU, deploy-like)", median(ra), mn(ra)))
+print(String(format: "  (B) pure GPU time   : median %.4f ms   min %.4f ms   (kernel only, no host)", median(gp), mn(gp)))

+// =============================================================================
+// melt_mpsgraph_opt.swift — MelT (MPSGraph) optimized "to the redline".
+// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Three levers vs the earlier exec script:
+//   1) PRE-ALLOCATED output  (results:[td], not nil)  -> kills per-call alloc
+//      that was inflating the host floor.
+//   2) fp16 path (--fp16)     -> Apple GPU runs half-precision ~2x faster; the
+//      matmul dominates, so this is the big GPU win on the edge. Changes
+//      precision -> the correctness diff vs fp32 is printed so you see the cost.
+//   3) max compilation optimization level.
+// Times (A) executable.run wall-clock and (B) pure GPU time (cmd-buffer stamps).
+//
+//   swift melt_mpsgraph_opt.swift            # fp32 (faithful)
+//   swift melt_mpsgraph_opt.swift --fp16     # edge-optimized
+//
+// NOTE: untested here. Risky API spots flagged // <-- CHECK.
+// Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  License: MIT.
+// =============================================================================
+import Foundation
+import Metal
+import MetalPerformanceShaders
+import MetalPerformanceShadersGraph
+
+let SR = 16000, N = 400, HOP = 160, M = 80
+let FMIN = 80.0, FMAX = 7600.0
+let EPS: Double = 1e-6
+let secs = 160.0
+let T = (Int(secs) * SR - N) / HOP + 1
+let useFp16 = CommandLine.arguments.contains("--fp16")
+let dt: MPSDataType = useFp16 ? .float16 : .float32
+let elemSize = useFp16 ? 2 : 4
+
+// --- bases (fp32 math) -> [Float] [N,2M] -------------------------------------
+func hz2mel(_ f: Double) -> Double { 2595.0 * log10(1.0 + f / 700.0) }
+func mel2hz(_ m: Double) -> Double { 700.0 * (pow(10.0, m / 2595.0) - 1.0) }
+func buildWriT() -> [Float] {
+    let lo = hz2mel(FMIN), hi = hz2mel(FMAX)
+    var freqs = [Double](repeating: 0, count: M)
+    for m in 0..<M { freqs[m] = mel2hz(lo + (hi - lo) * Double(m + 1) / Double(M + 1)) }
+    var win = [Double](repeating: 0, count: N)
+    for n in 0..<N { win[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2.0 * Double.pi * Double(n) / Double(N - 1)) }
+    var w = [Float](repeating: 0, count: N * 2 * M)
+    for n in 0..<N { for m in 0..<M {
+        let ph = 2.0 * Double.pi * freqs[m] * Double(n) / Double(SR)
+        w[n * 2 * M + m]     = Float(cos(ph) * win[n])
+        w[n * 2 * M + M + m] = Float(sin(ph) * win[n])
+    } }
+    return w
+}
+
+// fp32 array -> raw bytes in the chosen dtype (fp32 or fp16)
+func packed(_ a: [Float]) -> [UInt8] {
+    if !useFp16 { return a.withUnsafeBytes { Array($0) } }
+    let h = a.map { Float16($0) }
+    return h.withUnsafeBytes { Array($0) }                                   // <-- CHECK (Float16)
+}
+
+guard let device = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice() else { fatalError("no Metal device") }
+let queue = device.makeCommandQueue()!
+let mpsDevice = MPSGraphDevice(mtlDevice: device)
+
+let xF = (0..<(T * N)).map { _ in Float.random(in: -1...1) }
+let wF = buildWriT()
+let xBytes = packed(xF), wBytes = packed(wF)
+let xBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: xBytes, length: xBytes.count, options: .storageModeShared)!
+let wBuf = device.makeBuffer(bytes: wBytes, length: wBytes.count, options: .storageModeShared)!
+let outBuf = device.makeBuffer(length: T * M * elemSize, options: .storageModeShared)!   // PRE-ALLOC
+
+// --- graph -------------------------------------------------------------------
+let graph = MPSGraph()
+let x    = graph.placeholder(shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: dt, name: "x")
+let wriT = graph.placeholder(shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: dt, name: "wriT")
+let ri = graph.matrixMultiplication(primary: x, secondary: wriT, name: "proj")
+let r  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: 0, length: M, name: "r")     // <-- CHECK
+let i  = graph.sliceTensor(ri, dimension: 1, start: M, length: M, name: "i")     // <-- CHECK
+let s  = graph.addition(graph.square(with: r, name: "r2"),
+                        graph.square(with: i, name: "i2"), name: "s")
+let eps  = graph.constant(EPS, dataType: dt)                                     // <-- CHECK
+let melt = graph.logarithm(with: graph.addition(s, eps, name: "seps"), name: "melt")
+
+// --- compile (max optimization) ---------------------------------------------
+let comp = MPSGraphCompilationDescriptor()
+comp.optimizationLevel = .level1                                                 // <-- CHECK (max)
+let xST = MPSGraphShapedType(shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: dt)
+let wST = MPSGraphShapedType(shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: dt)
+let exe = graph.compile(with: mpsDevice, feeds: [x: xST, wriT: wST],
+                        targetTensors: [melt], targetOperations: nil,
+                        compilationDescriptor: comp)
+
+let xTD   = MPSGraphTensorData(xBuf,   shape: [T as NSNumber, N as NSNumber], dataType: dt)
+let wTD   = MPSGraphTensorData(wBuf,   shape: [N as NSNumber, (2 * M) as NSNumber], dataType: dt)
+let outTD = MPSGraphTensorData(outBuf, shape: [T as NSNumber, M as NSNumber], dataType: dt)   // PRE-ALLOC
+let byTensor: [MPSGraphTensor: MPSGraphTensorData] = [x: xTD, wriT: wTD]
+let inputs = (exe.feedTensors ?? [x, wriT]).map { byTensor[$0]! }
+
+func median(_ a: [Double]) -> Double { let s = a.sorted(); return s[s.count / 2] }
+
+// --- (A) executable.run wall-clock, PRE-ALLOCATED result --------------------
+let rd = MPSGraphExecutableExecutionDescriptor(); rd.waitUntilCompleted = true
+for _ in 0..<30 { _ = exe.run(with: queue, inputs: inputs, results: [outTD], executionDescriptor: rd) }
+var ra = [Double]()
+for _ in 0..<100 {
+    let t0 = DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds
+    _ = exe.run(with: queue, inputs: inputs, results: [outTD], executionDescriptor: rd)
+    ra.append(Double(DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds - t0) / 1e6)
+}
+
+// --- (B) pure GPU time ------------------------------------------------------
+var gp = [Double]()
+for k in 0..<130 {
+    let cb = queue.makeCommandBuffer()!
+    let mpscb = MPSCommandBuffer(commandBuffer: cb)
+    _ = exe.encode(to: mpscb, inputs: inputs, results: [outTD], executionDescriptor: nil)   // <-- CHECK
+    mpscb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
+    if k >= 30 { gp.append((cb.gpuEndTime - cb.gpuStartTime) * 1000.0) }
+}
+
+// --- correctness: row 0 vs fp32 Double reference ----------------------------
+var maxErr = 0.0
+let outP = outBuf.contents()
+for m in 0..<M {
+    var rr = 0.0, ii = 0.0
+    for n in 0..<N {
+        rr += Double(xF[n]) * Double(wF[n * 2 * M + m])
+        ii += Double(xF[n]) * Double(wF[n * 2 * M + M + m])
+    }
+    let ref = log(rr * rr + ii * ii + EPS)
+    let got = useFp16 ? Double(outP.load(fromByteOffset: m * 2, as: Float16.self))
+                      : Double(outP.load(fromByteOffset: m * 4, as: Float.self))
+    maxErr = max(maxErr, abs(got - ref))
+}
+
+print(String(format: "MelT MPSGraph OPT  X[%d,%d] M=%d (~%.0fs)  dtype=%@", T, N, M, secs, useFp16 ? "fp16" : "fp32"))
+print(String(format: "  (A) run (prealloc) : median %.4f ms   min %.4f ms", median(ra), ra.min()!))
+print(String(format: "  (B) pure GPU       : median %.4f ms   min %.4f ms", median(gp), gp.min()!))
+print(String(format: "  correctness row0   : max|Δ vs fp32| = %.2e", maxErr))

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# reproduce.sh — ONE command per box. Detects the platform, preflights, and runs
+# every speedup/energy stage eligible for this hardware.
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.  Output: results/raw/<id>/
+# Usage:  ./reproduce.sh [--platform h100|v100|m4pro|a18pro] [--check] [--force]
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+PLATFORM=""; CHECK=""; EXTRA=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
+  --platform) PLATFORM="$2"; shift 2;;
+  --check) CHECK="--check-only"; shift;;
+  --force) EXTRA="--force"; shift;;
+  *) echo "unknown arg: $1"; exit 2;;
+esac; done
+[ -z "$PLATFORM" ] && PLATFORM="$(python -m melt.detect)"
+echo "== MelT reproduce :: platform=$PLATFORM =="
+python -m melt.preflight --platform "$PLATFORM" ${CHECK:+--check-only}   # fail fast if not ready
+[ -n "$CHECK" ] && { echo "check-only: stopping."; exit 0; }
+python -m experiments.run --platform "$PLATFORM" --all $EXTRA
+python -m melt.env --platform "$PLATFORM" --out "results/raw/$PLATFORM/env.json"
+echo "DONE -> results/raw/$PLATFORM/   (rsync this folder to the collector box)"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# reproduce_spira.sh — CUDA-only task (accuracy/equivalence, NOT speedup).
+# Run ONCE on a CUDA box. Output: results/raw/tasks/   Produces: Table VII, Fig 6
+# Requires: datasets/spira (ACCESS-GATED, see data/spira.md)  +  requirements-tasks.txt
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT ...", IEEE Access 2026.
+#
+# By default this runs only the EVALUATION (assumes trained checkpoints exist
+# under datasets/spira/checkpoints/). Pass --train to first train BOTH front-end
+# variants (MFCC baseline via spira_mfcc_model + MFCCT via spira_mfcct_model),
+# which writes spira_final_model.pth and spira_mfcct_final_model.pth, then eval.
+#
+# Multi-seed robustness (Tier 2): --seeds 43,44,45,46,49 trains/evaluates per-seed
+# checkpoints and reports mean+/-std + a Wilcoxon paired test across seeds
+# (results/raw/tasks/spira_seeds*.csv). Combine with --train to train those seeds.
+#
+# Usage:  ./reproduce_spira.sh [--train] [--check] [--force] [--seeds 43,44,45,46,49]
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+CHECK=""; EXTRA=""; TRAIN=""; SEEDS=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
+  --train) TRAIN="1"; shift;;
+  --check) CHECK="--check-only"; shift;;
+  --force) EXTRA="--force"; shift;;
+  --seeds) SEEDS="$2"; shift 2;;
+  --seeds=*) SEEDS="${1#*=}"; shift;;
+  --multi-seed=*) SEEDS="${1#*=}"; shift;;
+  *) echo "unknown arg: $1"; exit 2;;
+esac; done
+SEEDARG=""; [ -n "$SEEDS" ] && SEEDARG="--seeds $SEEDS"
+
+echo "== MelT task :: spira (CUDA only) ${SEEDS:+[seeds=$SEEDS]} =="
+
+if [ -n "$TRAIN" ]; then
+  # train stage: needs the training CSV + audio (not checkpoints)
+  python -m melt.preflight --stage spira_train ${CHECK:+--check-only}
+  [ -z "$CHECK" ] && python -m experiments.run spira_train --tasks $EXTRA $SEEDARG
+fi
+
+# eval stage: needs the test CSV + audio + checkpoints
+python -m melt.preflight --stage spira ${CHECK:+--check-only}   # guards device=cuda + datasets + deps
+[ -n "$CHECK" ] && { echo "check-only: stopping."; exit 0; }
+python -m experiments.run spira --tasks $EXTRA $SEEDARG
+echo "DONE -> results/raw/tasks/   (Table VII, Fig 6)"

+
+def stft_mel_numpy(X, window, fb):
+    """Reference STFT+Mel on pre-framed X: log(|rFFT(X*win)|^2 @ fb^T).
+
+    rFFT over the LAST axis (frame samples) so the same code is correct for
+    2-D [T, frame_len] and batched 3-D [B, T, frame_len] inputs.
+    """
+    spec = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(X * window, axis=-1)) ** 2
+    return np.log(spec @ fb.T + EPS)
+
+
+def stft_mel_torch(X, window, fb):
+    """Torch mirror of stft_mel_numpy (rFFT over the last axis; batch-safe)."""
+    import torch
+    spec = torch.abs(torch.fft.rfft(X * window, dim=-1)) ** 2
+    return torch.log(spec @ fb.T + EPS)
+
+
+def make_reference(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max, backend, device=None):
+    """Build a callable STFT+Mel reference matched to the MelT configuration."""
+    window = dsp.hann(frame_len)
+    fb = dsp.mel_filterbank(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max)
+    if backend == "numpy":
+        return lambda X: stft_mel_numpy(X, window, fb)
+    if backend == "torch":
+        import torch
+        dev = torch.device(device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
+        w = torch.from_numpy(window).to(dev); f = torch.from_numpy(fb).to(dev)
+        return lambda X: stft_mel_torch(X, w, f)
+    raise ValueError(backend)
+
+
+def make_external(name, *, sr, n_fft, hop, n_mels, f_min, f_max, device):
+    """Return a torch callable for an external library, matched to our spec.
+
+    Supported: 'torchaudio', 'nnaudio', 'librosa'. Used only on CUDA/MPS for the
+    Table V comparison. Each returns log-Mel for parity with MelT.
+    """
+    import torch
+    name = name.lower()
+    if name == "torchaudio":
+        import torchaudio
+        mt = torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram(
+            sample_rate=sr, n_fft=n_fft, hop_length=hop, n_mels=n_mels,
+            f_min=f_min, f_max=f_max, power=2.0).to(device)
+        return lambda wav: torch.log(mt(wav) + EPS)
+    if name == "nnaudio":
+        try:                                    # nnAudio >= 0.3
+            from nnAudio.features.mel import MelSpectrogram as NNMel
+        except ImportError:                     # nnAudio < 0.3 (older layout)
+            from nnAudio.Spectrogram import MelSpectrogram as NNMel
+        nn = NNMel(sr=sr, n_fft=n_fft, hop_length=hop, n_mels=n_mels,
+                   fmin=f_min, fmax=f_max, verbose=False).to(device)
+        return lambda wav: torch.log(nn(wav.unsqueeze(0)) + EPS)
+    if name == "librosa":
+        import librosa
+        return lambda wav_np: np.log(librosa.feature.melspectrogram(
+            y=wav_np, sr=sr, n_fft=n_fft, hop_length=hop, n_mels=n_mels,
+            fmin=f_min, fmax=f_max, power=2.0) + EPS)
+    raise ValueError(f"unknown library: {name!r}")

+# =============================================================================
+# melt/detect.py — map THIS machine to a stable platform_id
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# Output filenames are namespaced by a controlled platform_id (h100/v100/m4pro/
+# a18pro), NOT by hostname or raw GPU string, so results never collide and stay
+# self-explanatory. `python -m melt.detect` prints the id (used by reproduce.sh
+# and the Makefile). Override anytime with --platform.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Detect the platform_id (h100/v100/m4pro/a18pro) of the current machine."""
+import platform
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+def gpu_name():
+    """Return the NVIDIA GPU name via nvidia-smi, or '' if none."""
+    try:
+        return subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name",
+                               "--format=csv,noheader"],
+                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+    except Exception:
+        return ""
+
+
+def apple_chip():
+    """Return the Apple SoC brand string on macOS, else ''."""
+    if platform.system() != "Darwin":
+        return ""
+    try:
+        return subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"],
+                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+    except Exception:
+        return ""
+
+
+def detect():
+    """Return the platform_id for this box (raises if unrecognised)."""
+    g = gpu_name().upper()
+    if "H100" in g:
+        return "h100"
+    if "V100" in g:
+        return "v100"
+    chip = apple_chip().upper()
+    if "A18" in chip:
+        return "a18pro"
+    if "M4" in chip:
+        return "m4pro"
+    raise SystemExit("could not detect platform; pass --platform "
+                     "{h100|v100|m4pro|a18pro}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    print(detect())

+# =============================================================================
+# melt/dsp.py — shared DSP primitives (Mel scale, window, framing, filterbank)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# These helpers are backend-agnostic (pure NumPy): they build the constant
+# matrices and frames that both the proposed frontend (melt.py) and the
+# conventional reference (baselines.py) consume. Keeping them in one place
+# guarantees MelT and STFT+Mel are compared under *identical* DSP parameters.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Backend-agnostic DSP helpers shared by MelT and the STFT+Mel baseline."""
+import math
+import numpy as np
+
+# --- Mel scale (HTK convention, as used throughout the paper) -----------------
+def hz_to_mel(f):
+    """Hertz -> Mel (HTK)."""
+    return 2595.0 * math.log10(1.0 + f / 700.0)
+
+def mel_to_hz(m):
+    """Mel -> Hertz (HTK inverse)."""
+    return 700.0 * (10.0 ** (m / 2595.0) - 1.0)
+
+def hann(n_win):
+    """Symmetric Hann window of length n_win (float32), == np.hanning(n_win).
+
+    Used by MelT, MFCCT, the STFT+Mel reference, and every task front end — one
+    window convention everywhere, no per-experiment variants.
+    """
+    n = np.arange(n_win, dtype=np.float64)
+    return (0.5 - 0.5 * np.cos(2.0 * math.pi * n / (n_win - 1))).astype(np.float32)
+
+def extract_frames(audio, frame_len, hop_len):
+    """Slice a 1-D signal into overlapping frames -> array [n_frames, frame_len].
+
+    Vectorised gather (no Python loop); matches the framing used in the paper's
+    benchmark so the per-clip frame count is identical across experiments.
+    """
+    audio = np.asarray(audio, dtype=np.float32)
+    n_frames = max(1, (len(audio) - frame_len) // hop_len + 1)
+    idx = np.arange(frame_len)[None, :] + hop_len * np.arange(n_frames)[:, None]
+    return audio[idx].astype(np.float32)
+
+# --- Constant matrices --------------------------------------------------------
+def meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max):
+    """Build the MelT projection matrices W_r, W_i  (shape [n_mels, frame_len]).
+
+    Columns are the windowed cosine/sine NDFT bases evaluated *directly* at the
+    Mel analysis frequencies. Those frequencies are defined CANONICALLY as the
+    CENTER frequencies of the standard triangular Mel filterbank — i.e. the n_mels
+    interior points of linspace(mel(f_min), mel(f_max), n_mels+2) (the same grid
+    librosa/HTK/torchaudio use for their filter apexes; see mel_filterbank() and
+    the Whisper-matched front end in experiments/tasks/whisper.py, which use the
+    identical [1:-1] grid). This makes MelT "the NDFT sampled at each Mel filter's
+    center," and keeps it aligned with the triangular bank it is compared against.
+    The (symmetric) Hann window is folded into the matrices so a single GEMM
+    (X @ W^T) performs windowing + projection at once.
+    """
+    mel_pts = np.linspace(hz_to_mel(f_min), hz_to_mel(f_max), n_mels + 2)[1:-1]
+    freqs = np.array([mel_to_hz(m) for m in mel_pts], dtype=np.float64)
+    n = np.arange(frame_len, dtype=np.float64)
+    win = hann(frame_len)
+    phase = 2.0 * math.pi * np.outer(freqs, n) / sr
+    w_r = (np.cos(phase) * win).astype(np.float32)
+    w_i = (np.sin(phase) * win).astype(np.float32)
+    return w_r, w_i
+
+def mel_filterbank(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max):
+    """Triangular Mel filterbank for the conventional STFT+Mel reference.
+
+    Shape [n_mels, frame_len//2 + 1]; matches librosa-style triangular weights.
+    """
+    n_freqs = frame_len // 2 + 1
+    mel_pts = np.linspace(hz_to_mel(f_min), hz_to_mel(f_max), n_mels + 2)
+    hz_pts = np.array([mel_to_hz(m) for m in mel_pts])
+    fbin = hz_pts / (sr / 2) * (n_freqs - 1)
+    fb = np.zeros((n_mels, n_freqs), dtype=np.float32)
+    for m in range(1, n_mels + 1):
+        lo, ctr, hi = fbin[m - 1], fbin[m], fbin[m + 1]
+        for k in range(n_freqs):
+            if lo < k < ctr:
+                fb[m - 1, k] = (k - lo) / (ctr - lo)
+            elif ctr <= k < hi:
+                fb[m - 1, k] = (hi - k) / (hi - ctr)
+    return fb
+
+def dct_ii_matrix(n_mfcc, n_mels):
+    """Orthonormal DCT-II matrix D (shape [n_mfcc, n_mels]) for MFCC/MFCCT."""
+    k = np.arange(n_mfcc)[:, None]
+    m = np.arange(n_mels)[None, :]
+    d = np.cos(math.pi * k * (2 * m + 1) / (2 * n_mels)).astype(np.float64)
+    d[0, :] *= 1.0 / math.sqrt(n_mels)
+    d[1:, :] *= math.sqrt(2.0 / n_mels)
+    return d.astype(np.float32)

+# =============================================================================
+# melt/env.py — capture the software/hardware environment (-> Table XIII)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# Every run drops a JSON sidecar with host, GPU/driver, and library versions so
+# the software table is GENERATED, never hand-typed. `analysis/aggregate.py`
+# rolls these into results/aggregated/environment.csv (Table XIII).
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Capture host/GPU/driver/library versions into a run.json / env.json sidecar."""
+import argparse
+import json
+import platform
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def _v(mod):
+    try:
+        return __import__(mod).__version__
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+def _dist(name):
+    """Version of an installed distribution by package name (not import name)."""
+    try:
+        import importlib.metadata as m
+        return m.version(name)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+def capture(platform_id=None):
+    """Return a dict describing the current environment.
+
+    If platform_id is not given, fall back to auto-detection so the sidecar is
+    always stamped (never null) even when env.py is invoked directly.
+    """
+    if platform_id is None:
+        try:
+            from .detect import detect
+            platform_id = detect()
+        except (Exception, SystemExit):     # detect() raises SystemExit if unknown
+            platform_id = None
+    info = {
+        "platform_id": platform_id,
+        "host": platform.node(),
+        "os": platform.platform(),
+        "python": platform.python_version(),
+        "numpy": _v("numpy"), "scipy": _v("scipy"),
+        "torch": _v("torch"), "mlx": _v("mlx"),
+        "torchaudio": _v("torchaudio"),
+        # NVML binding provenance: pynvml (deprecated) vs nvidia-ml-py matters
+        # for the energy-counter path; record whichever provides the `pynvml` import.
+        "nvidia_ml_py": _dist("nvidia-ml-py"),
+        "pynvml": _dist("pynvml"),
+    }
+    try:
+        info["gpu"] = subprocess.run(
+            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,driver_version",
+             "--format=csv,noheader"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+    except Exception:
+        info["gpu"] = None
+    return info
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="capture environment -> JSON")
+    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--platform", default=None)
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    p = Path(a.out); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    p.write_text(json.dumps(capture(a.platform), indent=2))
+    print(f"wrote {p}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# =============================================================================
+# melt/io.py — results schema + run.json provenance helpers
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT ...", IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# One tiny place that knows where results go and what provenance to stamp, so
+# every runner writes consistently: results/raw/<platform_id>/<stage>.csv (+ a
+# runs/<stage>.run.json sidecar). analysis/ reads only these conventions.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""Result paths, CSV writing, and per-run provenance sidecars."""
+import csv
+import json
+import subprocess
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]   # repo root (…/melt)
+RAW = ROOT / "results" / "raw"
+
+
+def _git_hash():
+    try:
+        return subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
+                              cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+def out_dir(platform_id=None, tasks=False):
+    """Directory for a stage's outputs: results/raw/<id>/ or results/raw/tasks/."""
+    d = RAW / ("tasks" if tasks else platform_id)
+    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    return d
+
+
+def write_csv(path, header, rows):
+    """Write a results CSV (header + rows)."""
+    path = Path(path)
+    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
+        w = csv.writer(f); w.writerow(header); w.writerows(rows)
+    return path
+
+
+def write_run_json(out, stage, platform_id, config, extra=None):
+    """Drop a provenance sidecar next to a stage's results."""
+    runs = Path(out) / "runs"; runs.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    from .env import capture
+    rec = {"stage": stage, "platform_id": platform_id, "git": _git_hash(),
+           "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
+           "config": str(config), "env": capture(platform_id)}
+    if extra:
+        rec.update(extra)
+    (runs / f"{stage}.run.json").write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2))

+# =============================================================================
+# melt/melt.py — THE CONTRIBUTION: MelT and MFCCT in one place
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Paper: Camargo & Finger, "MelT: GEMM-Native NDFT for Efficient Single-Stage
+#        Audio Frontends on Modern Accelerators," IEEE Access, 2026.
+#
+# MelT replaces the conventional STFT -> power -> Mel pipeline with a SINGLE
+# dense GEMM: a Mel-spaced Non-uniform DFT projection evaluated directly at the
+# Mel analysis frequencies. MFCCT is its cepstral extension (MelT followed by a
+# fixed DCT-II). Both share one Direct-Mel-Projection core and are kept in this
+# single file by design.
+#
+# Equations (paper, Sec. III):
+#   [R | I] = X [W_r ; W_i]^T            (single GEMM on CUDA; two GEMMs on MPS)
+#   S = R (.) R + I (.) I                 (Mel-spaced projection energy)
+#   MelT  = log(S + eps)
+#   MFCCT = MelT @ D^T                    (D = orthonormal DCT-II)
+#
+# Backends: 'numpy' (reference), 'torch' (CUDA/MPS, used for the paper timings),
+#           'mlx' (Apple). The torch path is what produces Tables IV/V/X/XI/XII.
+# License: MIT.
+# =============================================================================
+"""MelT and MFCCT — GEMM-native Mel / cepstral frontends (numpy/torch/mlx)."""
+import numpy as np
+from . import dsp
+
+EPS = 1e-6  # log-floor; identical across MelT, MFCCT and the STFT+Mel reference
+
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Functional core
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def direct_mel_projection(X, w_ri, n_mels):
+    """Shared core: S = R^2 + I^2 from a SINGLE fused GEMM.
+
+    The two projections R = X W_r^T and I = X W_i^T (Eq. 9) are evaluated as one
+    matmul against the stacked basis W_ri = [W_r; W_i] of shape
+    [2*n_mels, frame_len], then split into the two halves. This issues one kernel
+    launch and reads X once (instead of twice) and is mathematically identical to
+    the two separate projections.
+
+    `X`     : framed signal       [T, frame_len]
+    `w_ri`  : stacked MelT basis   [2*n_mels, frame_len]
+    Returns the Mel-spaced projection energy S  [T, n_mels].
+    """
+    RI = X @ w_ri.T                 # one GEMM -> [T, 2*n_mels]
+    R = RI[..., :n_mels]
+    I = RI[..., n_mels:]
+    return R * R + I * I
+
+
+def _project_split(X, w_r, w_i):
+    """S = R^2 + I^2 via two separate GEMMs.
+
+    Faster on Apple MPS / CPU, where the fused GEMM's wider output and the
+    strided slice of R, I cost more than two matmuls (measured: ~1.2x on A18).
+    Mathematically identical to direct_mel_projection.
+    """
+    R = X @ w_r.T
+    I = X @ w_i.T
+    return R * R + I * I
+
+
+def _prefer_fused(backend, device):
+    """Single fused GEMM wins on CUDA; two GEMMs win on Apple MPS / CPU / numpy."""
+    if backend != "torch":
+        return False
+    d = str(device or "")
+    if "cuda" in d:
+        return True
+    if "mps" in d or "cpu" in d:
+        return False
+    try:                                # device unspecified -> CUDA if one is present
+        import torch
+        return torch.cuda.is_available()
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+
+
+def melt(audio, *, sr=16000, frame_len=400, hop_len=160, n_mels=80,
+         f_min=80.0, f_max=7600.0, backend="numpy", device=None):
+    """Compute MelT features for a 1-D `audio` signal.
+
+    Returns log-compressed Mel-spaced projection energy [T, n_mels].
+    `backend` in {'numpy','torch','mlx'}; `device` is the torch device string.
+    """
+    w_r, w_i = dsp.meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max)
+    frames = dsp.extract_frames(audio, frame_len, hop_len)
+    if _prefer_fused(backend, device):
+        w_ri = np.concatenate([w_r, w_i], axis=0)    # stacked basis [2*n_mels, N]
+        xp, X, w_ri = _to_backend(backend, device, frames, w_ri)
+        S = direct_mel_projection(X, w_ri, n_mels)
+    else:
+        xp, X, w_r, w_i = _to_backend(backend, device, frames, w_r, w_i)
+        S = _project_split(X, w_r, w_i)
+    return xp.log(S + EPS)
+
+
+def mfcct(audio, *, sr=16000, frame_len=1200, hop_len=160, n_mels=128, n_mfcc=40,
+          f_min=0.0, f_max=8000.0, backend="numpy", device=None):
+    """Compute MFCCT features = MelT followed by an orthonormal DCT-II.
+
+    Defaults follow the paper's cepstral configuration (Table III).
+    Returns [T, n_mfcc].
+    """
+    w_r, w_i = dsp.meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max)
+    D = dsp.dct_ii_matrix(n_mfcc, n_mels)
+    frames = dsp.extract_frames(audio, frame_len, hop_len)
+    if _prefer_fused(backend, device):
+        w_ri = np.concatenate([w_r, w_i], axis=0)    # stacked basis [2*n_mels, N]
+        xp, X, w_ri, D = _to_backend(backend, device, frames, w_ri, D)
+        S = direct_mel_projection(X, w_ri, n_mels)
+    else:
+        xp, X, w_r, w_i, D = _to_backend(backend, device, frames, w_r, w_i, D)
+        S = _project_split(X, w_r, w_i)
+    M = xp.log(S + EPS)   # = MelT
+    return M @ D.T
+
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Thin OO wrappers (precompute constants once, apply many times — used in timing)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class MelT:
+    """Reusable MelT frontend: precompute bases once; __call__ is one fused GEMM
+    on CUDA, two GEMMs on MPS/CPU (the faster path per backend)."""
+    def __init__(self, *, sr=16000, frame_len=400, hop_len=160, n_mels=80,
+                 f_min=80.0, f_max=7600.0, backend="numpy", device=None):
+        self.cfg = dict(sr=sr, frame_len=frame_len, hop_len=hop_len, n_mels=n_mels,
+                        f_min=f_min, f_max=f_max, backend=backend, device=device)
+        w_r, w_i = dsp.meltf_weights(n_mels, frame_len, sr, f_min, f_max)
+        self.n_mels = n_mels
+        self.fused = _prefer_fused(backend, device)
+        if self.fused:
+            w_ri = np.concatenate([w_r, w_i], axis=0)   # stack once: [2*n_mels, N]
+            self.xp, self.w_ri = _to_backend(backend, device, w_ri)
+        else:
+            self.xp, self.w_r, self.w_i = _to_backend(backend, device, w_r, w_i)
+
+    def frames(self, audio):
+        """Pre-frame audio onto the configured backend/device (done once)."""
+        f = dsp.extract_frames(audio, self.cfg["frame_len"], self.cfg["hop_len"])
+        return _to_backend(self.cfg["backend"], self.cfg["device"], f)[1]
+
+    def __call__(self, X):
+        """Apply MelT to pre-framed input X (the hot path the timing harness loops)."""
+        if self.fused:
+            S = direct_mel_projection(X, self.w_ri, self.n_mels)
+        else:
+            S = _project_split(X, self.w_r, self.w_i)
+        return self.xp.log(S + EPS)
+
+
+class MFCCT(MelT):
+    """Reusable MFCCT frontend = MelT + fixed DCT-II."""
+    def __init__(self, *, n_mfcc=40, n_mels=128, frame_len=1200,
+                 f_min=0.0, f_max=8000.0, **kw):
+        super().__init__(n_mels=n_mels, frame_len=frame_len,
+                         f_min=f_min, f_max=f_max, **kw)
+        D = dsp.dct_ii_matrix(n_mfcc, n_mels)
+        self.D = _to_backend(self.cfg["backend"], self.cfg["device"], D)[1]
+
+    def __call__(self, X):
+        return super().__call__(X) @ self.D.T
+
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Backend dispatch (numpy / torch / mlx) — keeps the math above backend-free
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def _to_backend(backend, device, *arrays):
+    """Move numpy arrays onto the requested backend; return (xp, *arrays).

+    if backend == "numpy":
+        return (np, *[np.asarray(a) for a in arrays])
+    if backend == "torch":
+        import torch
+        dev = torch.device(device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
+        out = [torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(a)).to(dev) for a in arrays]
